#!/usr/bin/env bash
# tests/integration/orch-backend-misconfigured-test.sh
#
# SPEC-2 (#1801): Running with a backend configured as `sequential` (or any
# name that resolves to no plugin) fails the run as `misconfigured` naming the
# backend; the sequential fallback in `orch_load_backend` is removed.
#
# SPEC-4 (#1801): A configured backend plugin that is absent from the installed
# tree (not the checkout) fails the run as `misconfigured` naming the missing
# backend.
#
# SPEC-10 (#1801): A backend whose plugin directory is present but whose config
# file is unreadable (permissions, corrupt, or missing) fails the run as
# `misconfigured` naming the backend — tested from the installed tree.
#
# All three must FAIL on old code (which has the sequential fallback) and PASS
# on new code (which removes the fallback and returns 1 naming the backend).
#
# Old code behaviour under each SPEC:
#   SPEC-2: orch_load_backend "sequential" → hardcoded path to the fallback backend
#           via hardcoded path → sources it → returns 0.
#   SPEC-4: orch_load_backend "absent-backend" → _orch_find_backend_dir fails →
#           general sequential fallback fires → returns 0 with a warning.
#   SPEC-10: source on unreadable plugin.sh fails silently (no set -e in contract.sh) →
#            _ZBUILD_ORCH_BACKEND_LOADED=1 runs anyway → returns 0.
#
# New code: every case returns 1, _ZBUILD_ORCH_BACKEND_LOADED stays 0, and
# stderr names the backend.
#
# [#1801/SPEC-2] [#1801/SPEC-4] [#1801/SPEC-10]
set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)"

# shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/helpers.sh
source "$REPO_ROOT/scripts/lib/helpers.sh"
# shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/test-helpers.sh
source "$REPO_ROOT/scripts/lib/test-helpers.sh"

print_test_header "orch_load_backend fails misconfigured naming backend when fallback removed (#1801 SPEC-2,4,10)"
setup_test_env "orch-backend-misconfigured"

# Prevent auto-config-file reads from picking up the project's real config.
export ZBUILD_CONFIG_FILE="/dev/null"
export ZBUILD_PROJECT_ROOT="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/project"

# Source contract.sh — it auto-calls _orch_load_backend at end.
# With ZBUILD_PLUGINS_ROOT pointing at an empty dir and no zbuild_config_get_backend
# available, it defaults to "sequential" and:
#   old code: sources the fallback backend via hardcoded _ZBUILD_ROOT path → BACKEND_LOADED=1
#   new code: no fallback → orch_load_backend returns 1 (silenced by || true) → BACKEND_LOADED=0
# We reset _ZBUILD_ORCH_BACKEND_LOADED=0 before each SPEC section so the
# explicit call we are testing starts from a clean state.
_EMPTY_PLUGINS="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/empty-plugins"
mkdir -p "$_EMPTY_PLUGINS"
export ZBUILD_PLUGINS_ROOT="$_EMPTY_PLUGINS"
export ZBUILD_ORCHESTRATOR_BACKEND="sequential"

# shellcheck source=../../core/orch/contract.sh
source "$REPO_ROOT/core/orch/contract.sh"

# ── SPEC-2: "sequential" name resolves to no plugin (fallback removed) ───────
print_test_section "[#1801/SPEC-2] orch_load_backend 'sequential' fails when sequential fallback is removed"

_ZBUILD_ORCH_BACKEND_LOADED=0
export ZBUILD_PLUGINS_ROOT="$_EMPTY_PLUGINS"
_SPEC2_ERR=""
_SPEC2_RC=0
_SPEC2_ERR="$(orch_load_backend "sequential" 2>&1)" || _SPEC2_RC=$?

if [[ "$_SPEC2_RC" -ne 0 ]]; then
    assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-2] orch_load_backend 'sequential' returns non-zero (sequential fallback removed)"
else
    assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-2] orch_load_backend 'sequential' must return non-zero (sequential fallback removed)" \
        "returned 0; old code finds the fallback backend via hardcoded _ZBUILD_ROOT path and sources it"
fi

if [[ "${_ZBUILD_ORCH_BACKEND_LOADED:-0}" -ne 1 ]]; then
    assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-2] _ZBUILD_ORCH_BACKEND_LOADED is not 1 (backend correctly not loaded)"
else
    assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-2] _ZBUILD_ORCH_BACKEND_LOADED must not be 1 when backend failed to load" \
        "sentinel set to 1; old code sets it after sourcing the hardcoded sequential path"
fi

if grep -q 'sequential' <<< "$_SPEC2_ERR"; then
    assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-2] error output names the backend 'sequential'"
else
    assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-2] error output must name the backend 'sequential'" \
        "stderr did not contain 'sequential'; got: ${_SPEC2_ERR:-<empty>}"
fi

# The run must be reported as `misconfigured` (not a generic failure).
# New code emits "misconfigured" in its error message or sets
# _ZBUILD_ORCH_BACKEND_DISPOSITION=misconfigured; old code silently succeeds
# so this never reaches a misconfigured path at all.
if grep -q 'misconfigured' <<< "$_SPEC2_ERR" || \
   [[ "${_ZBUILD_ORCH_BACKEND_DISPOSITION:-}" == "misconfigured" ]]; then
    assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-2] backend failure is reported as 'misconfigured'"
else
    assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-2] backend failure must be reported as 'misconfigured'" \
        "neither error output nor _ZBUILD_ORCH_BACKEND_DISPOSITION contained 'misconfigured'; got: ${_SPEC2_ERR:-<empty>}"
fi

# ── SPEC-4: absent backend plugin fails naming the missing backend ─────────────
# Backend name that is not present in the empty ZBUILD_PLUGINS_ROOT and has no
# hardcoded fallback. Old code falls back to sequential silently; new code fails.
print_test_section "[#1801/SPEC-4] orch_load_backend absent plugin fails naming backend (no general fallback)"

_ZBUILD_ORCH_BACKEND_LOADED=0
export ZBUILD_PLUGINS_ROOT="$_EMPTY_PLUGINS"
_SPEC4_ERR=""
_SPEC4_RC=0
_SPEC4_ERR="$(orch_load_backend "orch-absent-spec4" 2>&1)" || _SPEC4_RC=$?

if [[ "$_SPEC4_RC" -ne 0 ]]; then
    assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-4] orch_load_backend absent plugin returns non-zero (no fallback)"
else
    assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-4] orch_load_backend absent plugin must return non-zero (no fallback)" \
        "returned 0; old code's general sequential fallback fires for any missing backend"
fi

if [[ "${_ZBUILD_ORCH_BACKEND_LOADED:-0}" -ne 1 ]]; then
    assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-4] _ZBUILD_ORCH_BACKEND_LOADED is not 1 (absent backend)"
else
    assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-4] _ZBUILD_ORCH_BACKEND_LOADED must not be 1 for absent backend" \
        "sentinel set to 1; old code's general fallback to sequential sets it"
fi

if grep -q 'orch-absent-spec4' <<< "$_SPEC4_ERR"; then
    assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-4] error output names the missing backend 'orch-absent-spec4'"
else
    assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-4] error output must name the missing backend 'orch-absent-spec4'" \
        "stderr: ${_SPEC4_ERR:-<empty>}"
fi

if grep -q 'misconfigured' <<< "$_SPEC4_ERR" || \
   [[ "${_ZBUILD_ORCH_BACKEND_DISPOSITION:-}" == "misconfigured" ]]; then
    assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-4] absent backend failure is reported as 'misconfigured'"
else
    assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-4] absent backend failure must be reported as 'misconfigured'" \
        "neither error output nor _ZBUILD_ORCH_BACKEND_DISPOSITION contained 'misconfigured'; got: ${_SPEC4_ERR:-<empty>}"
fi

# ── SPEC-10: present dir, unreadable plugin.sh — fails naming the backend ─────
# Plugin directory and manifest are present (discovery succeeds) but plugin.sh
# is unreadable (chmod 000), simulating a corrupt or permission-denied install.
#
# Old code: source on unreadable file fails silently (no set -e in contract.sh),
#   then sets _ZBUILD_ORCH_BACKEND_LOADED=1 and returns 0.
# New code: detects source failure, returns 1 naming the backend.
print_test_section "[#1801/SPEC-10] orch_load_backend unreadable plugin.sh fails naming backend"

_S10_PLUGINS="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/spec10-plugins"
_S10_PLUGIN_DIR="$_S10_PLUGINS/tool/orch-broken-spec10"
mkdir -p "$_S10_PLUGIN_DIR"
cat > "$_S10_PLUGIN_DIR/manifest.yaml" <<'MANIFEST'
id: orch-broken-spec10
name: Broken Backend Spec10
kind: tool
version: 0.0.1
provides:
  role: orchestrator-backend
  alias: orch-broken-spec10
MANIFEST
# Write a syntactically valid plugin.sh then remove read permission.
printf 'orch_spawn() { return 0; }\norch_capabilities() { printf '"'"'{}'"'"'; }\n' \
    > "$_S10_PLUGIN_DIR/plugin.sh"
chmod 000 "$_S10_PLUGIN_DIR/plugin.sh"

export ZBUILD_PLUGINS_ROOT="$_S10_PLUGINS"
_ZBUILD_ORCH_BACKEND_LOADED=0
_SPEC10_ERR=""
_SPEC10_RC=0
_SPEC10_ERR="$(orch_load_backend "orch-broken-spec10" 2>&1)" || _SPEC10_RC=$?

# Restore permissions so cleanup_test_env can remove the directory.
chmod 644 "$_S10_PLUGIN_DIR/plugin.sh" 2>/dev/null || true

if [[ "$_SPEC10_RC" -ne 0 ]]; then
    assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-10] orch_load_backend with unreadable plugin.sh returns non-zero"
else
    assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-10] orch_load_backend with unreadable plugin.sh must return non-zero" \
        "returned 0; old code: source fails silently, _ZBUILD_ORCH_BACKEND_LOADED=1 runs anyway, returns 0"
fi

if [[ "${_ZBUILD_ORCH_BACKEND_LOADED:-0}" -ne 1 ]]; then
    assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-10] _ZBUILD_ORCH_BACKEND_LOADED is not 1 (unreadable plugin.sh)"
else
    assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-10] _ZBUILD_ORCH_BACKEND_LOADED must not be 1 when plugin.sh unreadable" \
        "sentinel set to 1; old code sets it even when source fails"
fi

if grep -q 'orch-broken-spec10' <<< "$_SPEC10_ERR"; then
    assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-10] error output names the backend 'orch-broken-spec10'"
else
    assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-10] error output must name the backend 'orch-broken-spec10'" \
        "stderr: ${_SPEC10_ERR:-<empty>}"
fi

if grep -q 'misconfigured' <<< "$_SPEC10_ERR" || \
   [[ "${_ZBUILD_ORCH_BACKEND_DISPOSITION:-}" == "misconfigured" ]]; then
    assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-10] unreadable plugin.sh failure is reported as 'misconfigured'"
else
    assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-10] unreadable plugin.sh failure must be reported as 'misconfigured'" \
        "neither error output nor _ZBUILD_ORCH_BACKEND_DISPOSITION contained 'misconfigured'; got: ${_SPEC10_ERR:-<empty>}"
fi

cleanup_test_env
print_test_results
exit $((FAIL > 0))

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# tests/integration/orch-timeout-applies-test.sh

# sequential strategy stops at its stage template `timeout_s:` limit; the
# 300 s flat deadline no longer applies.
#
# Old code: every strategy calls
#   orch_collect "$pool_id" --timeout "${ZBUILD_ORCH_TIMEOUT:-300}"
# New code: every strategy calls
#   orch_collect "$pool_id" --timeout "$(template_stage_time_limit "$stage")"
#
# This test fails on old code (spy captures 300), passes on new code
# (spy captures the template's timeout_s: value).
#

set -uo pipefail

id: tpl-spec1
name: spec1 test
defaults:

testjob:
  roles: [testworker]
  timeout_s: 7

cat > "$_SPEC1_PLUGIN_DIR/manifest.yaml" <<'MF'
id: testworker
name: testworker
kind: agent
version: 0.0.1
hooks:
  run: testworker_run

  role: testworker
MF

        case "$1" in

    return 0
}
orch_spawn()    { return 0; }
orch_dispatch() { printf 'slot-%s\n' "$$"; return 0; }
orch_shutdown() { return 0; }

export ZBUILD_STATE_DIR="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/state"
mkdir -p "$ZBUILD_STATE_DIR"
printf '{"schema_version":1}' > "$ZBUILD_STATE_DIR/pipeline-state.json"
export ZBUILD_RUN_ID="spec1-test"
export ZBUILD_ORCH_SCRATCH="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/orch-scratch"
mkdir -p "$ZBUILD_ORCH_SCRATCH"

    "$ZBUILD_STATE_DIR/pipeline-state.json" \
    "$TEST_TEMP_DIR/plugins" 2>/dev/null || _s1a_rc=$?

    "$ZBUILD_STATE_DIR/pipeline-state.json" \
    "$TEST_TEMP_DIR/plugins" 2>/dev/null || _s1a2_rc=$?

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Guard: the orch-sequential plugin is removed from the installed tree (#1801,
# SPEC-3). A guard that passes while the directory still exists would let a
# trivially-present plugin defeat the whole point of SPEC-2's no-fallback rule.
#
# Two assertions:
#   1. The plugin directory itself does not exist in the installed tree.
#   2. No code or config file outside docs/adr/ still names "orch-sequential"
#      (the golden file, manifests, contract.sh hardcoded path, test references).
#
# Both must FAIL on current code (the directory exists and is referenced
# throughout) and PASS after the implementation removes the plugin.
#
# [#1801/SPEC-3]
set -uo pipefail

REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/../.." && pwd)"
source "$REPO_ROOT/scripts/lib/test-helpers.sh"

print_test_header "orch-sequential is absent from the installed tree (#1801 SPEC-3)"
setup_test_env "orch-sequential-absent-guard"

# ── SPEC-3a: plugin directory does not exist ─────────────────────────────────
_orch_seq_dir="$REPO_ROOT/plugins/tool/orch-sequential"
if [[ ! -d "$_orch_seq_dir" ]]; then
    assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-3] orch-sequential plugin directory does not exist"
else
    assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-3] orch-sequential plugin directory does not exist" \
        "directory still present: $_orch_seq_dir"
fi

# ── SPEC-3b: no code or config file outside docs/adr/ names orch-sequential ──
# Files allowed to reference orch-sequential: docs/adr/ (ADR prose)
# Files NOT allowed: core/, plugins/, scripts/, config/, tests/, .github/
_hits=""
while IFS= read -r _f; do
    # Skip docs/adr/ — ADR prose is allowed to name the deleted plugin
    case "$_f" in
        */docs/adr/*) continue ;;
        # Skip the guard test itself (this file)
        */orch-sequential-absent-guard-test.sh) continue ;;
    esac
    _hits="${_hits}${_f}"$'\n'
done < <(grep -rl "orch-sequential" \
    "$REPO_ROOT/core" \
    "$REPO_ROOT/plugins" \
    "$REPO_ROOT/scripts" \
    "$REPO_ROOT/config" \
    "$REPO_ROOT/tests" \
    "$REPO_ROOT/.github" \
    2>/dev/null || true)

# Remove trailing newline for display
_hits="${_hits%$'\n'}"
if [[ -z "$_hits" ]]; then
    assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-3] no code or config file outside docs/adr/ names orch-sequential"
else
    assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-3] no code or config file outside docs/adr/ names orch-sequential" \
        "still referenced in: $(printf '%s' "$_hits" | tr '\n' ' ')"
fi

print_test_results

2	# Guard: _orch_local_kill_slot and the always-run watchdog in runner.sh kill
3	# through zbuild_pg_kill, not through direct `kill` (#1801, SPEC-6).
4	#
5	# Direct `kill -TERM/-KILL $pid` only reaches the named process. A hook that
6	# forks a child which ignores TERM (as in SPEC-6b) keeps that child alive when
7	# the watchdog fires on just the leader. zbuild_pg_kill sends to the whole
8	# process group (TERM then KILL), so the child is caught.
9	#
10	# This is a static guard: it searches the source files for the patterns
11	# that must NOT be there (direct kill in _orch_local_kill_slot) and the
12	# patterns that MUST be there (zbuild_pg_kill call in both sites).
13	#
14	# The test must FAIL on current code (which uses direct kill in both places)
15	# and PASS after the implementation switches to zbuild_pg_kill.
16	#
17	# [#1801/SPEC-6]
18	set -uo pipefail
19	
20	REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/../.." && pwd)"
21	source "$REPO_ROOT/scripts/lib/test-helpers.sh"
22	
23	print_test_header "orch kill sites use zbuild_pg_kill (not direct kill) (#1801 SPEC-6)"
24	setup_test_env "orch-kill-uses-pg-kill-guard"
25	
26	LOCAL_ENGINE="$REPO_ROOT/core/orch/local_engine.sh"
27	RUNNER="$REPO_ROOT/core/pipeline/runner.sh"
28	
29	assert_file_exists "SPEC-0a: local_engine.sh exists" "$LOCAL_ENGINE"
30	assert_file_exists "SPEC-0b: runner.sh exists" "$RUNNER"
31	
32	# ── SPEC-6a: _orch_local_kill_slot calls zbuild_pg_kill ─────────────────────
33	# Extract the body of _orch_local_kill_slot (from its header to the closing }).
34	# After the fix it should call zbuild_pg_kill; on old code it calls direct kill.
35	_kill_slot_body="$(sed -n '/_orch_local_kill_slot\(\)/,/^}/p' "$LOCAL_ENGINE" 2>/dev/null || true)"
36	if grep -q 'zbuild_pg_kill' <<< "$_kill_slot_body"; then
37	    assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-6] _orch_local_kill_slot calls zbuild_pg_kill"
38	else
39	    assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-6] _orch_local_kill_slot calls zbuild_pg_kill" \
40	        "body uses direct kill; after #1801 it must call zbuild_pg_kill for process-group coverage"
41	fi
42	
43	# Old pattern: `kill -TERM/-KILL "$wrapper_pid"` individually (not zbuild_pg_kill).
44	# This must NOT appear in _orch_local_kill_slot after the fix.
45	if grep -qE 'kill\s+-TERM\s+"?\$wrapper_pid"?' <<< "$_kill_slot_body" || \
46	   grep -qE 'kill\s+-KILL\s+"?\$wrapper_pid"?' <<< "$_kill_slot_body"; then
47	    assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-6] _orch_local_kill_slot does not use bare kill on wrapper_pid" \
48	        "still uses direct \`kill -TERM/-KILL \$wrapper_pid\`; must use zbuild_pg_kill"
49	else
50	    assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-6] _orch_local_kill_slot does not use bare kill on wrapper_pid"
51	fi
52	
53	# ── SPEC-6b: always-run watchdog in runner.sh calls zbuild_pg_kill ──────────
54	# The always-run watchdog is inside _runner_dispatch_always_run. Extract its
55	# subshell block (from `_runner_dispatch_always_run` to the closing `done`).
56	_ar_body="$(sed -n '/_runner_dispatch_always_run()/,/^    }$/p' "$RUNNER" 2>/dev/null || true)"
57	if [[ -z "$_ar_body" ]]; then
58	    # fallback: grab from the function definition keyword to its end
59	    _ar_body="$(sed -n '/^    _runner_dispatch_always_run() {/,/^    }$/p' "$RUNNER" 2>/dev/null || true)"
60	fi
61	if grep -q 'zbuild_pg_kill' <<< "$_ar_body"; then
62	    assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-6] always-run watchdog in runner.sh calls zbuild_pg_kill"
63	else
64	    assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-6] always-run watchdog in runner.sh calls zbuild_pg_kill" \
65	        "_runner_dispatch_always_run uses direct kill; after #1801 the watchdog must call zbuild_pg_kill"
66	fi
67	
68	# ── SPEC-6c: zbuild_pg_kill is defined and sourced by both files ─────────────
69	PG_KILL_LIB="$REPO_ROOT/scripts/lib/proc-group.sh"
70	assert_file_exists "SPEC-6c: proc-group.sh defines zbuild_pg_kill" "$PG_KILL_LIB"
71	if grep -q 'zbuild_pg_kill()' "$PG_KILL_LIB" 2>/dev/null; then
72	    assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-6] zbuild_pg_kill is defined in proc-group.sh"
73	else
74	    assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-6] zbuild_pg_kill is defined in proc-group.sh" \
75	        "function not found in $PG_KILL_LIB"
76	fi
77	if grep -q 'proc-group' "$LOCAL_ENGINE" 2>/dev/null; then
78	    assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-6] local_engine.sh sources proc-group.sh (or its parent does)"
79	else
80	    assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-6] local_engine.sh sources proc-group.sh" \
81	        "no reference to proc-group.sh found in local_engine.sh"
82	fi
83	
84	# ── SPEC-6 runtime: TERM-ignoring child leaves no running process ─────────────
85	# Behavioral guarantee: after the watchdog kills a slot whose wrapper spawned a
86	# child that ignores TERM, that child must also be gone.
87	#
88	# Old _orch_local_kill_slot: `kill "-${sig}" "$wrapper_pid"` only. Killing the

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Guard: _orch_local_kill_slot and the always-run watchdog in runner.sh kill
# through zbuild_pg_kill, not through direct `kill` (#1801, SPEC-6).
#
# Direct `kill -TERM/-KILL $pid` only reaches the named process. A hook that
# forks a child which ignores TERM (as in SPEC-6b) keeps that child alive when
# the watchdog fires on just the leader. zbuild_pg_kill sends to the whole
# process group (TERM then KILL), so the child is caught.
#
# This is a static guard: it searches the source files for the patterns
# that must NOT be there (direct kill in _orch_local_kill_slot) and the
# patterns that MUST be there (zbuild_pg_kill call in both sites).
#
# The test must FAIL on current code (which uses direct kill in both places)
# and PASS after the implementation switches to zbuild_pg_kill.
#
# [#1801/SPEC-6]
set -uo pipefail

REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/../.." && pwd)"
source "$REPO_ROOT/scripts/lib/test-helpers.sh"

print_test_header "orch kill sites use zbuild_pg_kill (not direct kill) (#1801 SPEC-6)"
setup_test_env "orch-kill-uses-pg-kill-guard"

LOCAL_ENGINE="$REPO_ROOT/core/orch/local_engine.sh"
RUNNER="$REPO_ROOT/core/pipeline/runner.sh"

assert_file_exists "SPEC-0a: local_engine.sh exists" "$LOCAL_ENGINE"
assert_file_exists "SPEC-0b: runner.sh exists" "$RUNNER"

# ── SPEC-6a: _orch_local_kill_slot calls zbuild_pg_kill ─────────────────────
# Extract the body of _orch_local_kill_slot (from its header to the closing }).
# After the fix it should call zbuild_pg_kill; on old code it calls direct kill.
_kill_slot_body="$(sed -n '/_orch_local_kill_slot\(\)/,/^}/p' "$LOCAL_ENGINE" 2>/dev/null || true)"
if grep -q 'zbuild_pg_kill' <<< "$_kill_slot_body"; then
    assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-6] _orch_local_kill_slot calls zbuild_pg_kill"
else
    assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-6] _orch_local_kill_slot calls zbuild_pg_kill" \
        "body uses direct kill; after #1801 it must call zbuild_pg_kill for process-group coverage"
fi

# Old pattern: `kill -TERM/-KILL "$wrapper_pid"` individually (not zbuild_pg_kill).
# This must NOT appear in _orch_local_kill_slot after the fix.
if grep -qE 'kill\s+-TERM\s+"?\$wrapper_pid"?' <<< "$_kill_slot_body" || \
   grep -qE 'kill\s+-KILL\s+"?\$wrapper_pid"?' <<< "$_kill_slot_body"; then
    assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-6] _orch_local_kill_slot does not use bare kill on wrapper_pid" \
        "still uses direct \`kill -TERM/-KILL \$wrapper_pid\`; must use zbuild_pg_kill"
else
    assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-6] _orch_local_kill_slot does not use bare kill on wrapper_pid"
fi

# ── SPEC-6b: always-run watchdog in runner.sh calls zbuild_pg_kill ──────────
# The always-run watchdog is inside _runner_dispatch_always_run. Extract its
# subshell block (from `_runner_dispatch_always_run` to the closing `done`).
_ar_body="$(sed -n '/_runner_dispatch_always_run()/,/^    }$/p' "$RUNNER" 2>/dev/null || true)"
if [[ -z "$_ar_body" ]]; then
    # fallback: grab from the function definition keyword to its end
    _ar_body="$(sed -n '/^    _runner_dispatch_always_run() {/,/^    }$/p' "$RUNNER" 2>/dev/null || true)"
fi
if grep -q 'zbuild_pg_kill' <<< "$_ar_body"; then
    assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-6] always-run watchdog in runner.sh calls zbuild_pg_kill"
else
    assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-6] always-run watchdog in runner.sh calls zbuild_pg_kill" \
        "_runner_dispatch_always_run uses direct kill; after #1801 the watchdog must call zbuild_pg_kill"
fi

# ── SPEC-6c: zbuild_pg_kill is defined and sourced by both files ─────────────
PG_KILL_LIB="$REPO_ROOT/scripts/lib/proc-group.sh"
assert_file_exists "SPEC-6c: proc-group.sh defines zbuild_pg_kill" "$PG_KILL_LIB"
if grep -q 'zbuild_pg_kill()' "$PG_KILL_LIB" 2>/dev/null; then
    assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-6] zbuild_pg_kill is defined in proc-group.sh"
else
    assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-6] zbuild_pg_kill is defined in proc-group.sh" \
        "function not found in $PG_KILL_LIB"
fi
if grep -q 'proc-group' "$LOCAL_ENGINE" 2>/dev/null; then
    assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-6] local_engine.sh sources proc-group.sh (or its parent does)"
else
    assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-6] local_engine.sh sources proc-group.sh" \
        "no reference to proc-group.sh found in local_engine.sh"
fi

# ── SPEC-6 runtime: TERM-ignoring child leaves no running process ─────────────
# Behavioral guarantee: after the watchdog kills a slot whose wrapper spawned a
# child that ignores TERM, that child must also be gone.
#
# Old _orch_local_kill_slot: `kill "-${sig}" "$wrapper_pid"` only. Killing the
# wrapper with SIGKILL does not kill its children — they are orphaned and continue
# running. So a TERM-ignoring child outlives the watchdog on old code.
# New _orch_local_kill_slot: calls zbuild_pg_kill, which sends TERM then KILL to
# the WHOLE process group. The TERM-ignoring child receives KILL and exits.
#
# Fails on old code (child alive after collect kills wrapper).
# Passes on new code (process-group KILL reaches child).
print_test_section "[#1801/SPEC-6] TERM-ignoring child leaves no process after watchdog fires (runtime)"
# Source the implementations so the runtime paths execute (not just pattern-match).
# shellcheck source=../../core/orch/local_engine.sh
source "$REPO_ROOT/core/orch/local_engine.sh"
# shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/proc-group.sh
source "$REPO_ROOT/scripts/lib/proc-group.sh"

_s6rt_pool="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/spec6-rt-pool"
mkdir -p "$_s6rt_pool/pids" "$_s6rt_pool/results"
_s6rt_child_file="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/spec6-rt-child.pid"

# Start the wrapper as a NEW process group (set -m → background job is group leader).
# The wrapper forks a child that ignores TERM and records its PID. The wrapper
# itself waits and never writes a .exit file, so _orch_local_collect_results will
# time out and call _orch_local_kill_slot to kill the slot.
set -m
(
    ( trap '' TERM; printf '%s\n' "$BASHPID" > "$_s6rt_child_file"; sleep 120 ) &
    _s6rt_inner=$!
    trap ':' TERM
    wait "$_s6rt_inner" 2>/dev/null || true
) &
_s6rt_wrapper_pid=$!
set +m

printf '%s\n' "$_s6rt_wrapper_pid" > "$_s6rt_pool/pids/spec6rt.pid"
# No .inner_pid file: _orch_local_kill_slot only receives wrapper_pid, so the
# child can be reached only via process-group kill (the new code path).

# Wait for the child pid to be recorded (up to 5 s).
for _ in $(seq 1 50); do [[ -s "$_s6rt_child_file" ]] && break; sleep 0.1; done
_s6rt_child_pid="$(head -n 1 "$_s6rt_child_file" 2>/dev/null || true)"

# Collect with 2 s timeout. The wrapper never writes .exit, so collect fires the
# kill path. After collect returns, the child should be dead (new code) or alive (old).
_s6rt_rc=0
_orch_local_collect_results "$_s6rt_pool" "pids" 2 || _s6rt_rc=$?

# Poll briefly: the KILL signal needs a moment to be processed.
_s6rt_alive=1
if [[ -n "$_s6rt_child_pid" ]]; then
    for _ in $(seq 1 30); do
        kill -0 "$_s6rt_child_pid" 2>/dev/null || { _s6rt_alive=0; break; }
        sleep 0.1
    done
fi

if [[ -z "$_s6rt_child_pid" ]]; then
    assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-6] fixture: TERM-ignoring child recorded its pid" \
        "no pid written to $_s6rt_child_file (wrapper may not have started)"
elif [[ "$_s6rt_alive" -eq 1 ]]; then
    assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-6] TERM-ignoring child must not outlive the watchdog" \
        "pid $_s6rt_child_pid still alive; old code: direct kill misses TERM-ignoring children; new code: zbuild_pg_kill kills the group"
    kill -KILL "$_s6rt_child_pid" 2>/dev/null || true
    wait "$_s6rt_child_pid" 2>/dev/null || true
else
    assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-6] TERM-ignoring child does not outlive the watchdog (group kill via zbuild_pg_kill)"
fi

print_test_results

2	# Integration: #1831 — an `always_run:` stage runs on EVERY exit path.
3	#
4	# This is the assertion the attribute exists for. A mechanism that fires on four
5	# of five exit paths is #1878's defect wearing a new name ("the snapshot was
6	# never called"), so each path gets its own case and names itself on failure —
7	# a single parameterised assertion would report "one of five" and leave the
8	# operator to find which.
9	#
10	# Paths covered: rc=0, rc=1, a stage killed by SIGINT (rc=130 + the recorded
11	# abort word), SIGTERM to the runner, and a release hook that hangs past its
12	# own timeout_s.
13	set -euo pipefail

16	REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)"

21	# shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/test-helpers.sh
22	source "$REPO_ROOT/scripts/lib/test-helpers.sh"

24	print_test_header "always_run dispatches on every exit path (#1831)"
25	setup_test_env "zb-always-run-exit"
26	export ZBUILD_CONTRACT_VALIDATOR=warn

28	PLUGINS_ROOT="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/plugins"
29	export ZBUILD_PLUGINS_ROOT="$PLUGINS_ROOT"
30	export ZBUILD_EVENTS_DIR="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/events"
31	export ZBUILD_EVENTS_JSONL="$ZBUILD_EVENTS_DIR/events.jsonl"
32	export ZBUILD_EVENT_SCHEMA="$REPO_ROOT/config/event-schema.json"
33	export ZBUILD_MODELS_FILE="$REPO_ROOT/config/models.json"
34	export ZBUILD_CYCLES_ENABLED=0
35	export ZBUILD_SCOPE_OVERRIDE=1
36	mkdir -p "$ZBUILD_EVENTS_DIR" "$HOME/.zbuild"
37	printf '%s' "bootstrap" > "$HOME/.zbuild/scope-override-token"
38	
39	OVERLAY_REPO="$(setup_git_temp_repo always-run-overlay)"
40	install_template_overlay "$OVERLAY_REPO" always-run-minimal
41	
42	# The always-run plugin, bound by ROLE (not by directory — that coupling is
43	# what #1831 removes). It touches a marker so "did it run?" is a file test
44	# rather than an inference from an event that might not be emitted.
45	mock_plugin_factory "outcome"  "agent" 0 "" ""         >/dev/null
46	mock_plugin_factory "teardown" "tool"  0 "" "teardown" >/dev/null
47	
48	RELEASE_MARKER="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/release-ran"
49	RELEASE_ENTERED="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/release-entered"
50	_arm_release() {
51	    # Two markers, not one. ENTERED is written before the optional sleep,
52	    # RAN after it. With a single completion marker, "the watchdog killed a
53	    # hanging hook" and "the hook was never dispatched at all" are the same
54	    # observation — and SPEC-5 passed for that wrong reason during development,
55	    # before the dispatch worked at all.
56	    # $1 = optional `sleep N` injected between the two, for the watchdog case.

58	teardown_run() {
59	    : > "${RELEASE_ENTERED}"
60	    ${1:-:}

65	}
66	
67	# The stage announces that it is RUNNING (#2029). `pipeline-state.json` appears
68	# during startup, long before any stage is dispatched, so waiting on it and then
69	# sleeping a second is not "the stage has started" — it is a guess that happens to
70	# hold on an idle machine.
71	#
72	# On a loaded one it does not, and SPEC-4 then SIGTERMs a runner still setting up
73	# its worktree: no stage has run, no release hook is armed, no marker is written,
74	# and the assertion reports a missing file with no hint that the run never got

97	# Each case gets its own state dir: a stale marker or state file from a prior

120	# run holding process groups and locks nobody else will clean up.
121	print_test_section "[SPEC-2][change] release runs when a stage fails"
122	_arm_release; _arm_outcome "" 1
123	_run_case "rc1" skip

125	
126	# ─── [SPEC-3][change] the SIGINT path ─────────────────────────────────────
127	# #1850 (ADR-054 §4, ADR-025): the SIGINT path is the recorded abort word, not

183	# and it could never be diagnosed because "file not found" is the same output

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Integration: #1831 — an `always_run:` stage runs on EVERY exit path.
#
# This is the assertion the attribute exists for. A mechanism that fires on four
# of five exit paths is #1878's defect wearing a new name ("the snapshot was
# never called"), so each path gets its own case and names itself on failure —
# a single parameterised assertion would report "one of five" and leave the
# operator to find which.
#
# Paths covered: rc=0, rc=1, a stage killed by SIGINT (rc=130 + the recorded
# abort word), SIGTERM to the runner, and a release hook that hangs past its
# own timeout_s.
set -euo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)"
RUNNER="$REPO_ROOT/core/pipeline/runner.sh"

# shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/helpers.sh
source "$REPO_ROOT/scripts/lib/helpers.sh"
# shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/test-helpers.sh
source "$REPO_ROOT/scripts/lib/test-helpers.sh"

print_test_header "always_run dispatches on every exit path (#1831)"
setup_test_env "zb-always-run-exit"
export ZBUILD_CONTRACT_VALIDATOR=warn

PLUGINS_ROOT="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/plugins"
export ZBUILD_PLUGINS_ROOT="$PLUGINS_ROOT"
export ZBUILD_EVENTS_DIR="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/events"
export ZBUILD_EVENTS_JSONL="$ZBUILD_EVENTS_DIR/events.jsonl"
export ZBUILD_EVENT_SCHEMA="$REPO_ROOT/config/event-schema.json"
export ZBUILD_MODELS_FILE="$REPO_ROOT/config/models.json"
export ZBUILD_CYCLES_ENABLED=0
export ZBUILD_SCOPE_OVERRIDE=1
mkdir -p "$ZBUILD_EVENTS_DIR" "$HOME/.zbuild"
printf '%s' "bootstrap" > "$HOME/.zbuild/scope-override-token"

OVERLAY_REPO="$(setup_git_temp_repo always-run-overlay)"
install_template_overlay "$OVERLAY_REPO" always-run-minimal

# The always-run plugin, bound by ROLE (not by directory — that coupling is
# what #1831 removes). It touches a marker so "did it run?" is a file test
# rather than an inference from an event that might not be emitted.
mock_plugin_factory "outcome"  "agent" 0 "" ""         >/dev/null
mock_plugin_factory "teardown" "tool"  0 "" "teardown" >/dev/null

RELEASE_MARKER="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/release-ran"
RELEASE_ENTERED="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/release-entered"
_arm_release() {
    # Two markers, not one. ENTERED is written before the optional sleep,
    # RAN after it. With a single completion marker, "the watchdog killed a
    # hanging hook" and "the hook was never dispatched at all" are the same
    # observation — and SPEC-5 passed for that wrong reason during development,
    # before the dispatch worked at all.
    # $1 = optional `sleep N` injected between the two, for the watchdog case.
    cat > "$PLUGINS_ROOT/tool/teardown/plugin.sh" <<PLUG
teardown_run() {
    : > "${RELEASE_ENTERED}"
    ${1:-:}
    : > "${RELEASE_MARKER}"
    return 0
}
PLUG
}

# The stage announces that it is RUNNING (#2029). `pipeline-state.json` appears
# during startup, long before any stage is dispatched, so waiting on it and then
# sleeping a second is not "the stage has started" — it is a guess that happens to
# hold on an idle machine.
#
# On a loaded one it does not, and SPEC-4 then SIGTERMs a runner still setting up
# its worktree: no stage has run, no release hook is armed, no marker is written,
# and the assertion reports a missing file with no hint that the run never got
# that far. Observed directly — `wait` returned in 0s, the hook-entered marker was
# absent, and the runner's last line was "Working in the run's worktree".
#
# `runner-release-exit-paths-test.sh` already does this correctly with
# BUILD_STARTED; this is the same idea. The marker can only appear once the stage
# is genuinely executing, so load can only delay it, never fake it.
# #1850: the stage writes the v2 result its manifest (mock_plugin_factory's)
# promises — pass on rc 0, error/broken otherwise — so a run that should succeed
# is not failed for leaving no readable result.
_arm_outcome() {
    local _o=pass
    [[ "${2:-0}" -ne 0 ]] && _o=broken
    cat > "$PLUGINS_ROOT/agent/outcome/plugin.sh" <<PLUG
outcome_run() {
    : > "\${STAGE_STARTED:-/dev/null}"
    ${1:-:}
    $(mock_result_line outcome "$_o")
    return ${2:-0}
}
PLUG
}

# Each case gets its own state dir: a stale marker or state file from a prior
# case would make a later one pass for the wrong reason.
_run_case() {
    local name="$1" rc_want_set="$2"
    rm -f "$RELEASE_MARKER" "$RELEASE_ENTERED"
    export ZBUILD_STATE_DIR="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/state-$name"
    mkdir -p "$ZBUILD_STATE_DIR"
    set +e
    ( cd "$OVERLAY_REPO" && bash "$RUNNER" --template always-run-minimal \
        --goal "always-run $name" ) >"$TEST_TEMP_DIR/$name.out" 2>&1
    _CASE_RC=$?
    set -e
    [[ "$rc_want_set" == "skip" ]] || true
}

# ─── [SPEC-1][change] rc=0 — the ordinary success path ──────────────────────
print_test_section "[SPEC-1][change] release runs when the pipeline succeeds"
_arm_release; _arm_outcome "" 0
_run_case "rc0" skip
assert_file_exists "[SPEC-1] release ran on rc=0" "$RELEASE_MARKER"

# ─── [SPEC-2][change] rc=1 — a failed run still frees its resources ─────────
# The failing path is the one that matters most: a run that died is exactly the
# run holding process groups and locks nobody else will clean up.
print_test_section "[SPEC-2][change] release runs when a stage fails"
_arm_release; _arm_outcome "" 1
_run_case "rc1" skip
assert_file_exists "[SPEC-2] release ran on a non-zero stage rc" "$RELEASE_MARKER"

# ─── [SPEC-3][change] the SIGINT path ─────────────────────────────────────
# #1850 (ADR-054 §4, ADR-025): the SIGINT path is the recorded abort word, not
# rc=130 — a bare 130 from a stage is just a failed stage now. So the stage
# does what a Ctrl-C does to the process group: the sentinel is armed (empty =
# sigint) and the child dies with 130. The run must end on the abort path —
# exit 1, status interrupted — or this case would only repeat SPEC-2.
print_test_section "[SPEC-3][change] release runs on the SIGINT path (abort word sigint)"
_arm_release
# shellcheck disable=SC2016  # expanded by the stage at run time, not here
_arm_outcome ': > "$ZBUILD_STATE_DIR/.abort.signal"' 130
_run_case "rc130" skip
assert_file_exists "[SPEC-3] release ran on the SIGINT path" "$RELEASE_MARKER"
assert_eq "[SPEC-3] the run took the abort path: exit 1 (not 130), status interrupted" \
    "1 interrupted" "$_CASE_RC $(jq -r '.status // "MISSING"' "$TEST_TEMP_DIR/state-rc130/pipeline-state.json" 2>/dev/null)"

# ─── [SPEC-4][change] SIGTERM delivered to the runner itself ───────────────
# Distinct from SPEC-3: there the stage returned a code, here the signal is
# delivered to the runner process while a stage is still executing. #1759's
# re-armed INT/TERM traps are what give this path somewhere to hang off.
print_test_section "[SPEC-4][change] release runs when the runner is SIGTERMed mid-stage"
_arm_release; _arm_outcome "sleep 30" 0
rm -f "$RELEASE_MARKER" "$RELEASE_ENTERED"
export ZBUILD_STATE_DIR="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/state-sigterm"
export STAGE_STARTED="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/stage-started-sigterm"
rm -f "$STAGE_STARTED"
mkdir -p "$ZBUILD_STATE_DIR"
( cd "$OVERLAY_REPO" && bash "$RUNNER" --template always-run-minimal \
    --goal "always-run sigterm" ) >"$TEST_TEMP_DIR/sigterm.out" 2>&1 &
_runner_pid=$!
# Wait for the run to actually reach the stage before signalling — signalling a
# runner still in startup would prove nothing about the exit path.
#
# #2029: this used to wait for `pipeline-state.json` and then sleep 1. That file
# is written during STARTUP, so the wait proved nothing and the sleep was the only
# real margin. Under load it was not enough and the signal landed mid-startup.
# STAGE_STARTED is written by the stage itself, so it cannot be reached early.
_waited=0
while [[ ! -f "$STAGE_STARTED" && $_waited -lt 300 ]]; do
    sleep 0.2; _waited=$(( _waited + 1 ))
done
if [[ ! -f "$STAGE_STARTED" ]]; then
    assert_fail "[SPEC-4] the stage started before the signal was sent" \
        "STAGE_STARTED never appeared in 60s — the run never reached a stage, so the exit path was never exercised"
fi
_spec4_t0=$(date +%s)
kill -TERM "$_runner_pid" 2>/dev/null || true
wait "$_runner_pid" 2>/dev/null || true
_spec4_wait_s=$(( $(date +%s) - _spec4_t0 ))
# The trap runs in the dying process; give it a moment to land the marker.
_waited=0
while [[ ! -f "$RELEASE_MARKER" && $_waited -lt 50 ]]; do
    sleep 0.2; _waited=$(( _waited + 1 ))
done

# #2029: say WHAT WAS SEEN, not merely that the file is absent.
#
# This assertion has failed intermittently on CI for as long as it has existed,
# and it could never be diagnosed because "file not found" is the same output
# whether the runner ignored the signal, died before its trap, ran teardown into
# a different path, or simply had not finished yet. Three separate mechanisms
# were proposed for it and all three were disproven.
#
# The sibling assertion in runner-release-exit-paths prints the marker it read,
# and that one line is what let #2046 identify its cause in minutes after days of
# guessing. This is that lesson applied here: the next occurrence explains itself
# instead of starting another hunt.
if [[ ! -f "$RELEASE_MARKER" ]]; then
    {
        printf '  DIAGNOSTIC [SPEC-4]: release marker absent after %ss of polling\n' "$(( _waited * 2 / 10 ))"
        printf '    wait on the runner returned after: %ss\n' "$_spec4_wait_s"
        printf '    runner pid %s still alive: %s\n' "$_runner_pid" \
            "$(kill -0 "$_runner_pid" 2>/dev/null && echo YES || echo no)"
        printf '    release hook ENTERED marker: %s\n' \
            "$([[ -f "$RELEASE_ENTERED" ]] && echo present || echo absent)"
        printf '    state dir: %s\n' \
            "$([[ -d "$ZBUILD_STATE_DIR" ]] && (cd "$ZBUILD_STATE_DIR" && printf '%s ' * 2>/dev/null) || echo '<missing>')"
        printf '    runner output (last 5 lines):\n'
        tail -5 "$TEST_TEMP_DIR/sigterm.out" 2>/dev/null | sed 's/^/      /' || printf '      <no output>\n'
    } >&2
fi
# RELEASE_ENTERED separates "the hook never started" from "it started and did not
# finish" — the single most useful split, and the one the bare check cannot make.
assert_file_exists "[SPEC-4] release ran after SIGTERM to the runner" "$RELEASE_MARKER"

# ─── [SPEC-5][guard] a hanging release cannot hang the exit ────────────────
# The stage declares timeout_s: 2. A hook that blocks past it must be killed and
# the exit must continue — otherwise Ctrl-C becomes a lockup, which is the exact
# class of bug an EXIT-trap dispatch exists to avoid. Asserting the WALL CLOCK
# rather than the marker: the marker would also be absent if release never ran
# at all, so it cannot distinguish "bounded" from "broken".
print_test_section "[SPEC-5][guard] a release hook that hangs is bounded by its timeout_s"
_arm_release "sleep 60"; _arm_outcome "" 0
rm -f "$RELEASE_MARKER" "$RELEASE_ENTERED"
export ZBUILD_STATE_DIR="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/state-hang"
mkdir -p "$ZBUILD_STATE_DIR"
_t0=$(date +%s)
set +e
( cd "$OVERLAY_REPO" && bash "$RUNNER" --template always-run-minimal \
    --goal "always-run hang" ) >"$TEST_TEMP_DIR/hang.out" 2>&1
set -e
_elapsed=$(( $(date +%s) - _t0 ))
# 45s is generous against a 2s bound plus runner startup; the assertion is
# "bounded at all", not a tight budget — a tight one would flake under a loaded
# parallel pool (the #991 lesson).
if [[ "$_elapsed" -lt 45 ]]; then
    assert_pass "[SPEC-5] a 60s release hook did not hold the exit (${_elapsed}s)"
else
    assert_fail "[SPEC-5] a 60s release hook held the exit" "elapsed=${_elapsed}s"
fi
# These two together are what make the case meaningful: the hook WAS entered
# (so the bound is what stopped it) and did NOT complete (so it was actually
# killed). Either alone is satisfied by a dispatch that never happened.
assert_file_exists "[SPEC-5] the hanging hook was actually dispatched" "$RELEASE_ENTERED"
assert_file_not_exists "[SPEC-5] the hanging hook was killed before completing" "$RELEASE_MARKER"

# ─── [SPEC-6][guard] an unresolvable always-run role is LOUD ───────────────
# The code this replaces did `[[ -d "$_td_dir" ]] || return 0` — a missing
# plugin was a silent no-op. An always-run stage that cannot be resolved has not
# run, and the operator must be able to see that rather than infer it from a
# missing effect.
print_test_section "[SPEC-6][guard] an unresolvable role emits an event instead of failing silently"
_arm_outcome "" 0
rm -f "$RELEASE_MARKER"
rm -rf "$PLUGINS_ROOT/tool/teardown"
export ZBUILD_STATE_DIR="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/state-unresolved"
export ZBUILD_EVENTS_JSONL="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/events/unresolved.jsonl"
mkdir -p "$ZBUILD_STATE_DIR"
set +e
( cd "$OVERLAY_REPO" && bash "$RUNNER" --template always-run-minimal \
    --goal "always-run unresolved" ) >"$TEST_TEMP_DIR/unresolved.out" 2>&1
_unres_rc=$?
set -e
assert_event_emitted "[SPEC-6] stage.always_run.unresolved is emitted" \
    "$ZBUILD_EVENTS_JSONL" "stage.always_run.unresolved"
# And it must not change the run's fate — an always-run stage never decides the
# verdict, including when it could not be found.
assert_eq "[SPEC-6] an unresolvable always-run stage does not fail the run" "0" "$_unres_rc"

print_test_results

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# scripts/lib/lint-test-errexit.sh — #2252 G
#
# A test file that runs without stop-on-error (its first `set -…` line has no
# `e`) must not turn it on later: from that line every assertion that expects a
# non-zero rc kills the file instead of being checked. #1844's test-author
# wrapped a call in `set +e … set -e` inside a `set -uo pipefail` file and the
# next expected rc=1 aborted it. A file that starts with -e may toggle it.
#
# Usage: bash scripts/lib/lint-test-errexit.sh [root]   (default: the repo)
# Exit:  0 = clean; 1 = at least one offending file.
set -euo pipefail

_LTE_ROOT="${1:-$(cd "${BASH_SOURCE[0]%/*}" 2>/dev/null || true; cd "../.." && pwd)}"
_bad=0
while IFS= read -r -d '' f; do
    [[ "$f" == */legacy-DoNotUse/* ]] && continue
    # One awk pass: the header is the first `set -<flags>` line of the file's own
    # shell; heredoc bodies are skipped — a fixture script written by the test is
    # not the test's own shell (its `set -e` is the fixture's business).
    while IFS=$'\t' read -r ln header; do
        [[ -n "$ln" ]] || continue
        echo "lint-test-errexit: ${f#"$_LTE_ROOT"/}:$ln turns stop-on-error on in a file that runs without it (header: ${header:-none}) — an expected non-zero rc after this line kills the file; use 'cmd || rc=\$?' instead" >&2
        _bad=$((_bad + 1))
    done < <(awk '
        doc != "" { t = $0; sub(/^\t+/, "", t); if (t == doc) doc = ""; next }
        /^[[:space:]]*#/ { next }
        # The line itself is judged BEFORE a heredoc it opens hides what follows:
        # a set -e on the opening line belongs to the test shell (review #2253).
        !seen && /^set -[a-zA-Z]+/ {
            seen = 1; hdr = $0; f = $2; sub(/^-/, "", f)
            haserr = (f ~ /e/); next
        }
        seen && !haserr && /^[[:space:]]*set -[a-zA-Z]*e[a-zA-Z]*([[:space:]]|$)/ { print NR "\t" hdr }
        {
            line = $0
            if (match(line, /<<-?[[:space:]]*["\047]?[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*["\047]?/)) {
                d = substr(line, RSTART, RLENGTH); sub(/^<<-?[[:space:]]*/, "", d); gsub(/["\047]/, "", d)
                if (line !~ /<<</) doc = d
            }
        }
    ' "$f" 2>/dev/null)
done < <(find "$_LTE_ROOT/tests" "$_LTE_ROOT/plugins" -name '*-test.sh' -print0 2>/dev/null)

if (( _bad > 0 )); then
    echo "lint-test-errexit: $_bad file(s) switch stop-on-error on mid-file" >&2
    exit 1
fi
echo "lint-test-errexit: clean"

```awk
!seen && /^set -[a-zA-Z]+/ {
    seen = 1; hdr = $0; f = $2; sub(/^-/, "", f)
    haserr = (f ~ /e/); next
}
seen && !haserr && /^[[:space:]]*set -[a-zA-Z]*e[a-zA-Z]*([[:space:]]|$)/ { print NR "\t" hdr }
```

So it flags any later `set` line containing `-e` if the file's first `set` line didn't have it. For `always-run-exit-paths-test.sh`, line 13 starts with `set -euo pipefail`, which already includes `-e`, so that's fine. #!/usr/bin/env bash
# Integration test (#1829, ADR-054 §7): the runner dispatches cleanup(release)
# on EVERY exit path from a run — success, non-zero rc, the SIGINT propagation
# chain, an external SIGTERM, and an external timeout.
#
# This is the acceptance criterion the mechanism exists for: a stage's live
# resources must be freed however the run ends. A single missed exit path leaks
# whatever that stage spawned (#1748: suites observed alive 15+ min after exit).
#
# Why SIGINT is driven by the stage rather than `kill -INT`: this harness starts
# non-interactively with SIGINT inherited as SIG_IGN, and POSIX forbids a child
# from un-ignoring it — so `kill -INT` is silently dropped and the assertion
# would pass standalone while proving nothing. The repo's existing
# sigint-aborts-pipeline-test.sh drives the same chain the same way: the child
# returns 130, which is exactly what the kernel produces on Ctrl-C. Since #1850
# (ADR-054 §4, ADR-025) a signal is a recorded WORD, not an rc, so the stage
# also arms the abort sentinel (empty = sigint), as the runner's INT trap in
# the process group would.
#
# Assertion in every case: the stub stages' cleanup hooks recorded `release`
# (and never `purge`) in the marker file.
set -euo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)"
RUNNER="$REPO_ROOT/core/pipeline/runner.sh"

# shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/helpers.sh
source "$REPO_ROOT/scripts/lib/helpers.sh"
# shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/test-helpers.sh
source "$REPO_ROOT/scripts/lib/test-helpers.sh"

print_test_header "runner dispatches cleanup(release) on every exit path (#1829)"
setup_test_env "runner-release-exit-paths"
export ZBUILD_CONTRACT_VALIDATOR=warn

PLUGINS_ROOT="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/plugins"
export ZBUILD_PLUGINS_ROOT="$PLUGINS_ROOT"
export ZBUILD_EVENT_SCHEMA="$REPO_ROOT/config/event-schema.json"
export ZBUILD_MODELS_FILE="$REPO_ROOT/config/models.json"
export ZBUILD_CYCLES_ENABLED=0
mkdir -p "$PLUGINS_ROOT"

# The teardown plugin resolves its repo root by walking three levels up from
# its own directory (plugin-bootstrap), using a LOGICAL pwd — so symlinking the
# plugin itself would resolve to TEST_TEMP_DIR and fail to find helpers.sh.
# Give TEST_TEMP_DIR the shape of a repo root instead, then copy teardown in.
ln -s "$REPO_ROOT/scripts" "$TEST_TEMP_DIR/scripts"
ln -s "$REPO_ROOT/core"    "$TEST_TEMP_DIR/core"
mkdir -p "$PLUGINS_ROOT/tool"
cp -R "$REPO_ROOT/plugins/tool/teardown" "$PLUGINS_ROOT/tool/teardown"

mock_plugin_factory "intake" "agent" 0 >/dev/null
mock_plugin_factory "build"  "agent" 0 >/dev/null
mock_plugin_factory "test"   "tool"  0 >/dev/null

# Declare the optional cleanup hook — without it plugin_hook_call emits
# `plugin.cleanup.absent`, returns 0 (#1823: rc is binary), and the stage is a
# no-op rather than a witness.
# Re-emit the manifest rather than appending: `cleanup:` has to sit inside the
# contiguous `hooks:` block, and mock_plugin_factory already wrote `requires:`
# after it. #1850/#2366: the re-emitted manifest keeps the factory's declaration —
# result_contract 3 and a JSON primary each run hook below writes.
for _spec in "agent/intake:intake:intake_cleanup" "agent/build:build:build_cleanup" "tool/test:test:test_cleanup"; do
    _dir="${_spec%%:*}"; _rest="${_spec#*:}"; _id="${_rest%%:*}"; _fn="${_rest#*:}"
    _kind="${_dir%%/*}"
    cat > "$PLUGINS_ROOT/$_dir/manifest.yaml" <<EOF
id: $_id
name: Test $_id
kind: $_kind
version: 0.0.1
hooks:
  run: ${_id//-/_}_run
  cleanup: $_fn
requires:
  core:
    - redaction
provides:
  result_contract: 3
outputs:
  - id: ${_id//-/_}_result
    path: \${artifact_dir}/${_id}-result.json
    type: ${_id}-result.json@1
    format: json
    required: true
    primary: true
EOF
done

# Stubs: run honours env-driven rc/sleep; cleanup records "<stage>:<scope>".
cat > "$PLUGINS_ROOT/agent/intake/plugin.sh" <<'PLUG'
intake_run() {
    local _art; _art="${ZBUILD_ARTIFACT_DIR:-$(dirname "$2")/artifacts}"; mkdir -p "$_art"
    printf '%s' '{"result_contract":3,"outcome":"pass","reason":"stub"}' > "$_art/intake-result.json"
    return 0
}
intake_cleanup() { printf 'intake:%s\n' "${3:-NOSCOPE}" >> "${RELEASE_MARKER}"; return 0; }
PLUG
cat > "$PLUGINS_ROOT/agent/build/plugin.sh" <<'PLUG'
build_run() {

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# ╔═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗
# ║  zBuild test-helpers — Shared test harness for all unit tests        ║
# ║  Source this from any *-test.sh file to get assert_*, setup, teardown    ║
# ╚═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝
#
# Usage:
#   SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "${BASH_SOURCE[0]%/*}" 2>/dev/null || true; pwd)"
#   source "$SCRIPT_DIR/lib/test-helpers.sh"
#
# Provides:
#   Colors, counters, assert_pass/fail/eq/contains/contains_regex/gt/json_key
#   setup_test_env / cleanup_test_env  (temp dir, mock PATH, mock HOME)
#   print_test_header / print_test_results
#   Mock helpers: mock_binary, mock_jq, mock_git, mock_gh, mock_claude

[[ -n "${_TEST_HELPERS_LOADED:-}" ]] && return 0
_TEST_HELPERS_LOADED=1

# ─── Re-entrancy guard (#971): refuse a test invoked inside another test run ──
# Every *-test.sh sources this file first, so this is the universal chokepoint.
# A test executed from WITHIN another test run — e.g. the ablation negctl/
# reachability gates run `bash <changed-test>` directly — would re-enter the gate
# logic and fork-bomb the pipeline test stage (the recurring #929/#983/#971 class).
# The #983 guard in run-tests.sh only catches run-tests.sh-mediated nesting; the
# ablation's direct `bash` bypasses it. This guard catches BOTH paths.
# The sentinel has NO leading underscore so env-scrub's ^(ZBUILD_|_TPL_) clears it
# at every fresh-user-shell boundary (the pipeline test stage), avoiding a stale-
# value false refusal. Fixture-isolated nested runs set ZBUILD_TESTS_DIR and are
# exempt (mirrors the #983 guard's exemption). The guard fires ONLY when $0 is a
# `*-test.sh` being EXECUTED (`bash <test>.sh` — the ablation/fork-bomb path), not
# when a script merely sources this file for introspection (`bash -c "source …"`,
# where $0 is `bash`) — so test-helpers' own self-tests are unaffected.
if [[ -n "${ZBUILD_TEST_EXEC_ACTIVE:-}" && -z "${ZBUILD_TESTS_DIR:-}" && "${0##*/}" == *-test.sh ]]; then
    echo "test-helpers.sh: refusing nested test invocation (re-entrancy guard #971)" >&2
    exit 2
fi
export ZBUILD_TEST_EXEC_ACTIVE=1

# The vision admission gate (ADR-049 / #1360) enforces a conforming vision doc by
# default. Fixture-based tests spin up temp repos with no vision doc and are not
# testing vision, so they must opt out — same hermeticity precedent as
# ZBUILD_CONTRACT_VALIDATOR. Tests that DO exercise the gate set the mode inline
# per-case, which overrides this default. Real (non-test) runs never source this
# file, so dogfood-on-zbuild still enforces against the real .zbuild/vision.md.
export ZBUILD_VISION_GATE="${ZBUILD_VISION_GATE:-off}"

# ─── Colors ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
CYAN='\033[38;2;0;212;255m'
GREEN='\033[38;2;74;222;128m'
RED='\033[38;2;248;113;113m'
# shellcheck disable=SC2034
YELLOW='\033[38;2;250;204;21m'
# shellcheck disable=SC2034
PURPLE='\033[38;2;168;85;247m'
DIM='\033[2m'
BOLD='\033[1m'
RESET='\033[0m'

# ─── Counters ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
PASS=0
FAIL=0
TOTAL=0
SKIP=0
FAILURES=()

# ─── Auto-initialize TEST_TEMP_DIR ──────────────────────────────────────────
# Many test files use TEST_TEMP_DIR in their setup_env() without calling
# setup_test_env(). Auto-create a temp dir so $TEST_TEMP_DIR is never empty.
# Save originals now so cleanup_test_env() can always restore them.
ORIG_HOME="${HOME}"
ORIG_PATH="${PATH}"
# Sandbox ZBUILD_STATE_DIR and ZBUILD_ARTIFACT_DIR so stage-io writes during
# tests never escape to the outer pipeline's state directory (#1713).
# `+set` records SET-ness separately from the value: `${VAR:-}` collapses "unset"
# and "set but empty" into the same "", and cleanup would then unset a variable
# the caller had deliberately exported as empty. `${VAR-}` (no colon) keeps an
# empty value as empty.
ORIG_STATE_DIR_SET="${ZBUILD_STATE_DIR+set}"
ORIG_STATE_DIR="${ZBUILD_STATE_DIR-}"

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# Tests: orch-mock orch_collect honors the orch contract — 0/1 plus the partial word (PR #269, #1850) — issue #277
3	# Sibling backends (orch-bash-parallel, orch-ruflo-hive) were
4	# normalised in #269; orch-mock was missed. This test guards the fix.
5	set -euo pipefail
6	
7	SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
8	REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/../../../.." && pwd)"
9	
10	source "$REPO_ROOT/scripts/lib/helpers.sh"
11	source "$REPO_ROOT/scripts/lib/test-helpers.sh"
12	
13	print_test_header "orch-mock — orch_collect returns 0/1 and names partial per orch contract"
14	
15	setup_test_env "plugin-orch-mock"
16	export ORCH_MOCK_DIR="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/orch-mock"
17	
18	# shellcheck source=../../../../plugins/tool/orch-mock/plugin.sh
19	source "$REPO_ROOT/plugins/tool/orch-mock/plugin.sh"
20	
21	# ─── M1: all-pass → 0 ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
22	pool="m1-all-pass"
23	orch_spawn "$pool" 3 ""
24	orch_dispatch "$pool" "$(orch_work_unit 'exit 0')" >/dev/null
25	orch_dispatch "$pool" "$(orch_work_unit 'exit 0')" >/dev/null
26	orch_dispatch "$pool" "$(orch_work_unit 'exit 0')" >/dev/null
27	set +e
28	orch_collect "$pool" >/dev/null
29	rc=$?
30	set -e
31	if [[ $rc -eq 0 ]]; then
32	    assert_pass "M1: all-pass returns 0 (got $rc)"
33	else
34	    assert_fail "M1: all-pass returns 0" "got $rc"
35	fi
36	orch_shutdown "$pool"
37	
38	# ─── M2: all-fail → 1 ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
39	# First exit code is intentionally NOT 1 — pre-fix code returned the first
40	# non-zero rc encountered, so if the first failure were 1 this assertion
41	# would pass on the buggy version. Putting 5 first makes the test
42	# discriminating: only the normaliser can return 1 here.
43	pool="m2-all-fail"
44	orch_spawn "$pool" 3 ""
45	orch_dispatch "$pool" "$(orch_work_unit 'exit 5')" >/dev/null
46	orch_dispatch "$pool" "$(orch_work_unit 'exit 2')" >/dev/null
47	orch_dispatch "$pool" "$(orch_work_unit 'exit 7')" >/dev/null
48	set +e
49	orch_collect "$pool" >/dev/null
50	rc=$?
51	set -e
52	if [[ $rc -eq 1 ]]; then
53	    assert_pass "M2: all-fail returns 1 (got $rc) — not raw rc passthrough (pre-fix would have returned 5)"
54	else
55	    assert_fail "M2: all-fail returns 1" "got $rc (pre-fix would have returned 5, the first non-zero)"
56	fi
57	orch_shutdown "$pool"
58	
59	# ─── M3: mixed → 2 ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
60	pool="m3-mixed"
61	orch_spawn "$pool" 3 ""
62	orch_dispatch "$pool" "$(orch_work_unit 'exit 0')" >/dev/null
63	orch_dispatch "$pool" "$(orch_work_unit 'exit 1')" >/dev/null
64	orch_dispatch "$pool" "$(orch_work_unit 'exit 0')" >/dev/null
65	set +e
66	orch_collect "$pool" >/dev/null
67	rc=$?
68	set -e
69	# #1850 (ADR-054 §4): rc 1, and the partial-failure signal is the word.
70	assert_eq "M3: mixed returns 1" "1" "$rc"
71	assert_eq "M3: mixed is named partial" "partial" "${_ORCH_COLLECT_OUTCOME:-}"
72	orch_shutdown "$pool"
73	
74	# ─── M4: empty pool → 0 ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
75	pool="m4-empty"
76	orch_spawn "$pool" 1 ""
77	set +e
78	orch_collect "$pool" >/dev/null
79	rc=$?
80	set -e
81	if [[ $rc -eq 0 ]]; then
82	    assert_pass "M4: empty pool returns 0 (got $rc)"
83	else
84	    assert_fail "M4: empty pool returns 0" "got $rc"
85	fi
86	orch_shutdown "$pool"
87	
88	
89	# ─── M5 [#1801/SPEC-11]: pool isolation — two concurrent pools do not bleed ──
90	# Two pools are spawned independently and each dispatches its own work units.
91	# Collect on each pool must return only that pool's results: the passing pool
92	# returns 0 and the failing pool returns 1, with no cross-contamination.
93	# Fails if orch_collect drains a shared queue instead of a per-pool queue.
94	pool_pass="m5-pool-pass"
95	pool_fail="m5-pool-fail"
96	orch_spawn "$pool_pass" 2 ""
97	orch_spawn "$pool_fail" 2 ""
98	
99	# Dispatch only passing work to pool_pass, only failing work to pool_fail.
100	orch_dispatch "$pool_pass" "$(orch_work_unit 'exit 0')" >/dev/null
101	orch_dispatch "$pool_pass" "$(orch_work_unit 'exit 0')" >/dev/null
102	orch_dispatch "$pool_fail" "$(orch_work_unit 'exit 1')" >/dev/null
103	orch_dispatch "$pool_fail" "$(orch_work_unit 'exit 1')" >/dev/null
104	
105	set +e
106	orch_collect "$pool_pass" >/dev/null
107	rc_pass=$?
108	orch_collect "$pool_fail" >/dev/null
109	rc_fail=$?
110	set -e
111	
112	if [[ $rc_pass -eq 0 ]]; then

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Tests: orch-mock orch_collect honors the orch contract — 0/1 plus the partial word (PR #269, #1850) — issue #277
# Sibling backends (orch-bash-parallel, orch-ruflo-hive) were
# normalised in #269; orch-mock was missed. This test guards the fix.
set -euo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/../../../.." && pwd)"

source "$REPO_ROOT/scripts/lib/helpers.sh"
source "$REPO_ROOT/scripts/lib/test-helpers.sh"

print_test_header "orch-mock — orch_collect returns 0/1 and names partial per orch contract"

setup_test_env "plugin-orch-mock"
export ORCH_MOCK_DIR="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/orch-mock"

# shellcheck source=../../../../plugins/tool/orch-mock/plugin.sh
source "$REPO_ROOT/plugins/tool/orch-mock/plugin.sh"

# ─── M1: all-pass → 0 ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
pool="m1-all-pass"
orch_spawn "$pool" 3 ""
orch_dispatch "$pool" "$(orch_work_unit 'exit 0')" >/dev/null
orch_dispatch "$pool" "$(orch_work_unit 'exit 0')" >/dev/null
orch_dispatch "$pool" "$(orch_work_unit 'exit 0')" >/dev/null
set +e
orch_collect "$pool" >/dev/null
rc=$?
set -e
if [[ $rc -eq 0 ]]; then
    assert_pass "M1: all-pass returns 0 (got $rc)"
else
    assert_fail "M1: all-pass returns 0" "got $rc"
fi
orch_shutdown "$pool"

# ─── M2: all-fail → 1 ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# First exit code is intentionally NOT 1 — pre-fix code returned the first
# non-zero rc encountered, so if the first failure were 1 this assertion
# would pass on the buggy version. Putting 5 first makes the test
# discriminating: only the normaliser can return 1 here.
pool="m2-all-fail"
orch_spawn "$pool" 3 ""
orch_dispatch "$pool" "$(orch_work_unit 'exit 5')" >/dev/null
orch_dispatch "$pool" "$(orch_work_unit 'exit 2')" >/dev/null
orch_dispatch "$pool" "$(orch_work_unit 'exit 7')" >/dev/null
set +e
orch_collect "$pool" >/dev/null
rc=$?
set -e
if [[ $rc -eq 1 ]]; then
    assert_pass "M2: all-fail returns 1 (got $rc) — not raw rc passthrough (pre-fix would have returned 5)"
else
    assert_fail "M2: all-fail returns 1" "got $rc (pre-fix would have returned 5, the first non-zero)"
fi
orch_shutdown "$pool"

# ─── M3: mixed → 2 ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
pool="m3-mixed"
orch_spawn "$pool" 3 ""
orch_dispatch "$pool" "$(orch_work_unit 'exit 0')" >/dev/null
orch_dispatch "$pool" "$(orch_work_unit 'exit 1')" >/dev/null
orch_dispatch "$pool" "$(orch_work_unit 'exit 0')" >/dev/null
set +e
orch_collect "$pool" >/dev/null
rc=$?
set -e
# #1850 (ADR-054 §4): rc 1, and the partial-failure signal is the word.
assert_eq "M3: mixed returns 1" "1" "$rc"
assert_eq "M3: mixed is named partial" "partial" "${_ORCH_COLLECT_OUTCOME:-}"
orch_shutdown "$pool"

# ─── M4: empty pool → 0 ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
pool="m4-empty"
orch_spawn "$pool" 1 ""
set +e
orch_collect "$pool" >/dev/null
rc=$?
set -e
if [[ $rc -eq 0 ]]; then
    assert_pass "M4: empty pool returns 0 (got $rc)"
else
    assert_fail "M4: empty pool returns 0" "got $rc"
fi
orch_shutdown "$pool"


# ─── M5 [#1801/SPEC-11]: pool isolation — two concurrent pools do not bleed ──
# Two pools are spawned independently and each dispatches its own work units.
# Collect on each pool must return only that pool's results: the passing pool
# returns 0 and the failing pool returns 1, with no cross-contamination.
# Fails if orch_collect drains a shared queue instead of a per-pool queue.
pool_pass="m5-pool-pass"
pool_fail="m5-pool-fail"
orch_spawn "$pool_pass" 2 ""
orch_spawn "$pool_fail" 2 ""

# Dispatch only passing work to pool_pass, only failing work to pool_fail.
orch_dispatch "$pool_pass" "$(orch_work_unit 'exit 0')" >/dev/null
orch_dispatch "$pool_pass" "$(orch_work_unit 'exit 0')" >/dev/null
orch_dispatch "$pool_fail" "$(orch_work_unit 'exit 1')" >/dev/null
orch_dispatch "$pool_fail" "$(orch_work_unit 'exit 1')" >/dev/null

set +e
orch_collect "$pool_pass" >/dev/null
rc_pass=$?
orch_collect "$pool_fail" >/dev/null
rc_fail=$?
set -e

if [[ $rc_pass -eq 0 ]]; then
    assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-11] pool isolation: passing pool collect returns 0 (not contaminated by failing pool)"
else
    assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-11] pool isolation: passing pool collect must return 0" \
        "got $rc_pass — results from the failing pool may have bled into the passing pool"
fi
if [[ $rc_fail -eq 1 ]]; then
    assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-11] pool isolation: failing pool collect returns 1 (not contaminated by passing pool)"
else
    assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-11] pool isolation: failing pool collect must return 1" \
        "got $rc_fail — results from the passing pool may have bled into the failing pool"
fi
orch_shutdown "$pool_pass"
orch_shutdown "$pool_fail"

cleanup_test_env

id: simple
name: Simple Pipeline
extends: null

# ADR-037 §4: per-template merge policy. Wired to runtime behavior in #975.
merge_policy: auto_unless_flagged

# #2367: the run's branch; {key} is the run's identity (issue-<n>). A repository
# overrides it in .zbuild/branch; ZBUILD_WORKSPACE_BRANCH overrides both.
branch: zbuild/{key}

defaults:
  strategy: map

# ─── Flow ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Simplified pipeline (ADR-037 EPIC #966 / ADR-040 EPIC #1129): 7 top-level flow
# units — intake, plan, design, build_test_cycle, review_lenses,
# pr — where build_test_cycle groups the build/test leaves plus the decomposed
# mechanical gate stages, and review_lenses is the advisory lens group.
#
# I10-A..C historically wrapped build/test/objective-gate in build_test_cycle.
# B6 (#1138, ADR-040 — amends ADR-013/ADR-021/ADR-019; executes ADR-037 §6) CUT
# OVER convergence from the retired monolithic objective-gate to the composable
# mechanical gates; the objective-gate plugin was then removed in B7 (#1139).
# #2368: the engine combines the gates by build_test_cycle's exit_when, which
# names every member that must pass; gate-aggregator is retired.
#
# C3 (#1142, ADR-040 §3 — supersedes ADR-038's single-stage fan-out; ADR-039
# parallel group; follows ADR-030 scope governance) CUTS OVER the lens side: the
# monolithic `review` stage (ADR-038's hand-rolled review-report fan-out, now
# UNREFERENCED here) is replaced by `review_lenses` — a `type: map over: lenses`
# `aggregate: advisory` group (issue #1295, ADR-047 §2; was `type: parallel`) —
# one work unit per lens element. #2368: the engine sums the lenses up
# (review_lenses-summary.md) and says whether one was flagged
# (ZBUILD_RUN_FLAGGED); review-aggregator is retired. The lens group is
# ADVISORY: it NEVER feeds the cycle's
# exit_when/convergence (build_test_cycle's exit_when, ADR-040 §5) and never
# blocks merge. The B5 no-LLM-on-convergence-path invariant therefore holds.
flow:
  - hydrate
  - intake
  - plan
  - delivery_loop
  - review_lenses
  - pr

# ─── always_run (#1831) ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Stages that run on EVERY exit path — success, non-zero rc, SIGINT, SIGTERM,
# timeout — in the order listed, after the flow has ended.
#
# This replaces a hardcoded dispatch in the runner's EXIT trap, which named one
# plugin by DIRECTORY (`plugins/tool/teardown`) and degraded silently to a no-op
# if it was absent. "Runs on every exit path" is a property of the FLOW, so it
# belongs in the template that defines the flow — not at a line number inside a
# 3000-line runner, where an edit can drop it without anything noticing. #1878
# found exactly that failure in the sibling mechanism: the snapshot was never
# called.
#
# An always-run stage is NOT part of `flow:` and never enters the flow's stage
# list: it has no place in the pipeline's data dependencies and must not affect
# convergence, verdicts, or the run's exit status.
#
# Each entry is an ordinary top-level stage section — resolved by `roles:` like
# any other stage, and bounded by its own `router.timeout_s`. A name here with
# no section, or a section with no `roles:`, REFUSES the template rather than
# quietly running nothing.
always_run:
  - release
  - persist

# ─── delivery_loop (cycle) — #2271, ADR-068 ─────────────────────────────────
# One outer loop holds design and the build loop. Every stage sees every
# finding and says in its own result what it did about each; the engine never
# decides who owns a finding, and nothing jumps backwards.
#   - design makes one model call per run and checks the design it wrote. One
#     that fails is `unusable`: the engine runs design again (its retry:), and
#     each run starts from the last good design and the last try's failures
#     (ADR-068 §8). A design that still fails ends the run — stop_run_on_fail:
#     build never runs on it, and another round would only repeat those tries.
delivery_loop:
  type: cycle
  description: Design, then build, until both pass — going round when a finding needs design
  flow:
    - design
    - build_test_cycle
  exit_when:
    all:
      - { stage: design, field: verdict, op: eq, value: pass }
      - { stage: build_test_cycle, field: verdict, op: eq, value: pass }
  stop_run_on_fail: [design]
  max_iterations: 2
  on_max: halt

# ─── test-author (leaf, build_test_cycle member; the loop requires it) ───────
# ADR-040 §5: it makes a model call, so it may not sit on the convergence path.
# Its work is verified mechanically downstream — the test stage runs the
# assertions and acceptance-gate proves they discriminate.
test-author:
  gate: auto
  roles: [test_author]
  # The whole stage, every call and check inside it (4 model calls of 15 minutes, plus a few minutes); the engine
  # stops it here. The default for a stage is 900 (15 minutes).
  timeout_s: 3780
  # #2188: no authored assertions → the cycle stops before build. Otherwise build
  # writes its own tests, the defect #2022 exists to prevent (#1849 run
  # 35949629759). Its failure is retried first (the stage's `retry:` budget).
  blocking: true
  router:
    # #2188: the same budget as build — authoring a 15–25 SPEC contract is
    # build-sized work (#1849: two 600s calls both timed out mid-write).
    # #2225: per CALL now — test-author loops until it says it is done, like
    # build, so a big contract takes more calls instead of overrunning one.
    # At most 4 calls: timeouts that are not back-to-back let the loop go on,
    # so the ceiling is calls × timeout — 60 min here (review #2229).
    timeout_s: 900
    max_turns: 0
    max_iterations: 4

# ─── issue-acceptance (leaf, gate) ───────────────────────────────────────────
# #1849: the finished change against the ISSUE. A model call on the convergence
# path is allowed for the same reason as design's coverage check (ADR-040 §5 as amended by
# #2040): its standard is the issue, which the judged stages cannot re-author.
issue-acceptance:
  gate: auto
  roles: [issue_acceptance]
  # Same question design's coverage check asks of the design — "was what was asked for
  # delivered?" — now asked of the code.
  persona: product-owner
  router:
    timeout_s: 600

# ─── build_test_cycle (cycle) ────────────────────────────────────────────────
# B6 (#1138, ADR-040 §2/§5): the cycle re-runs build/test then the decomposed
# mechanical gates. #2368: the engine combines them — exit_when names every
# member that must pass this round; one with no outcome this round counts as
# failed (the ADR-019 fail-closed contract). gate-aggregator is retired.
# (#1129 Change C, ADR-012: the lint/coverage/mutation read-out gates were
# DROPPED as cycle members — they were redundant. mutation and lint both run in
# the test suite (run-tests.sh --tier all / npm test, which the `test` cycle
# member runs), so a lint or mutation regression fails the `test` gate directly.
# coverage is NOT folded into the suite — it stays enforced by the dedicated CI
# `coverage` job (re-running it inside --tier all would trip the #983 re-entrancy
# guard; see ADR-012 "Coverage gating"). The lint-gate/coverage-gate/mutation-gate
# plugins remain canonical (ADR-013) but dormant for future reuse.)
# The individual gates are NON-blocking (no blocking:true):
# they emit verdict-in-artifact (ADR-004) and the cycle iterates-to-fix; the loop
# converges via exit_when, never via per-gate hard-blocks. max_iterations: 3.
# Nested in delivery_loop (#2271): running out of rounds hands back to that loop,
# which goes round from design.
build_test_cycle:
  type: cycle
  description: Build, test, and run the mechanical gates until every one passes
  flow:
    # #2022: test-author runs FIRST. It authors the acceptance assertions from
    # the design's SPEC sentences before build implements against them, so the
    # code and the assertion are two independent readings rather than two
    # artifacts of one. It never sees the diff. #2370: it then checks each
    # assertion tests what its SPEC says (was spec-correspondence), and the loop
    # requires it to pass — the SPEC is design's, which it cannot re-author.
    - test-author
    # #2371: build scans its own change for secrets (was a stage of its own).
    - build
    - test
    # #1849: the finished change judged against the ISSUE, not the SPECs — the
    # only check after design's own coverage check that reads the issue; each unmet
    # requirement is a numbered finding.
    - issue-acceptance
  exit_when:
    all:
      - { stage: test-author, field: verdict, op: eq, value: pass }
      # #2371: build must pass — it scans its own change for secrets, and a
      # build that broke scope or did not finish is not done either.
      - { stage: build, field: verdict, op: eq, value: pass }
      - { stage: test, field: verdict, op: eq, value: pass }
      - { stage: issue-acceptance, field: verdict, op: eq, value: pass }
  max_iterations: 3
  on_max: continue
# ─── intake (leaf) ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
intake:
  gate: auto
  roles: [intake]
  io:
    destinations: [file, stdout]
    tail_lines: 200

# ─── plan (leaf) ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
plan:
  gate: auto
  roles: [planner]
  # ADR-051: the provider runs the stage as this persona (--agent).
  persona: product-owner
  io:
    destinations: [file, stdout]
    tail_lines: 200
  router:
    timeout_s: 300
    # 45 (raised from the 25 default, #1442): scope exploration needs
    # headroom. The planner is
    # also told this budget in its prompt and biased to converge before it runs out.
    max_turns: 45

# ─── design (leaf, delivery_loop member) ───────────────────────────────
design:
  gate: auto
  roles: [designer]
  # The whole stage, every call and check inside it (one 20-minute design call
  # and a 20-minute coverage call, plus a few minutes); the engine stops it
  # here. Each run is a new stage, with its own limit. The default is 900.
  timeout_s: 2700
  # ADR-068 §8: a run whose design cannot be used is run again, handed its
  # failures and the last good design — 3 runs in all.
  retry: 2
  # ADR-051: the provider runs the stage as this persona (--agent).
  persona: architect
  io:
    destinations: [file, stdout]
    tail_lines: 200
  router:
    # #1944: three 600s calls in a row ran out of time on a resumed run.
    timeout_s: 1200
    max_turns: 0

# ─── build (leaf, cycle member) ──────────────────────────────────────────────
build:
  gate: auto
  roles: [builder]
  # The whole stage, every call and check inside it (3 rounds of 15-minute model calls, and more); the engine
  # stops it here. The default for a stage is 900 (15 minutes).
  timeout_s: 3600
  # ADR-051: the provider runs the stage as this persona (--agent).
  persona: developer
  io:
    destinations: [file, stdout]
    tail_lines: 200
  router:
    timeout_s: 900
    max_turns: 0

# ─── test (leaf, cycle member) ───────────────────────────────────────────────
test:
  gate: auto
  roles: [tester]
  # #2372: test runs the shape floor and the acceptance check over its own run,
  # and checks the assertion files against their fingerprints. ADR-036 #1188:
  # negctl_timeout_s bounds each requirement's negative-control / reachability
  # run (seconds).
  negctl_timeout_s: 60
  # The whole stage, every call and check inside it (the full test suite); the engine
  # stops it here. The default for a stage is 900 (15 minutes).
  timeout_s: 2700
  io:
    destinations: [file, stdout]
    tail_lines: 200

# ─── review_lenses (map group, ADVISORY) ─────────────────────────────────────
# issue #1295 (ADR-047 §2): converted from `type: parallel` to `type: map`.
# Each element (security, performance, red-team, correctness, scope) becomes one
# work unit dispatched to the review-lens plugin (provides.role: review_lens).
# `as: ZBUILD_REVIEW_LENS_ID` maps each element into the env var the review-lens
# plugin already reads to derive the lens identity — so the plugin is unchanged
# from its per-stage form. This eliminates the five separate lens-* stage
# definitions while preserving the same five isolated LLM calls and the same
# lens-<element>.json artifact names (ADR-038 §2 isolated-call discipline).
#
# aggregate: advisory — this group is NEVER on a merge-blocking path (ADR-040 §4).
# Convergence is owned by build_test_cycle's exit_when above;
# the B5 (#1137) no-LLM-on-convergence-path invariant therefore holds.
review_lenses:
  type: map
  # #2368: a lens fails on a problem the change introduced of these severities.
  fail_on: [high, critical]
  over: lenses
  # ADR-051 §2: each lens names the persona it runs as; none is inferred
  # from the lens's name.
  elements:
    - id: security
      persona: security
    - id: performance
      persona: performance
    - id: red-team
      persona: red-team
    - id: correctness
      persona: correctness
    - id: scope
      persona: scope
    - id: sre
      persona: sre
  roles: [review_lens]
  as: ZBUILD_REVIEW_LENS_ID
  max_parallel: 4
  on_member_error: continue
  aggregate: advisory
  io:
    destinations: [file]
    tail_lines: 200
  router:
    timeout_s: 300
    max_turns: 25

# ─── pr (leaf) ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# T0 tool stage (ADR-013): opens the pull request; no LLM call.
pr:
  gate: auto
  roles: [pr]
  io:
    destinations: [file, stdout]
    tail_lines: 200

# ─── release (always-run, ADR-054 §7) ────────────────────────────────────────
# Frees live resources — process groups, locks, handles — and DELETES NOTHING,
# so a failed run keeps every byte of its evidence on disk. The teardown plugin
# pins its own scope to `release`; `purge` is operator-only and unreachable from
# any run path (`zbuild clean --purge`).
#
# timeout_s is 30 and is load-bearing, not a formality: this stage runs inside
# the EXIT trap, so a cleanup hook that blocks would turn Ctrl-C into a hang —
# the exact class of bug the mechanism exists to prevent.
release:
  gate: auto
  roles: [teardown]
  timeout_s: 30
  router:
    timeout_s: 30
  io:
    destinations: [file]
    tail_lines: 50

# ─── persist (always-run, ADR-050 §7 / ADR-059 §3) ───────────────────────────
# Snapshots the artifact area to zbuild/state/issue-<N> and PUSHES it, on every
# exit path. Runs AFTER release, and that order is load-bearing: release frees
# live resources and must stay fast, while this does network I/O and can block
# on auth or a dead remote. Persist last means a bad network can never delay an
# abort.

# timeout_s is 120, four times release's 30. A push crosses the network; a
# process-group kill does not.
persist:
  gate: auto
  roles: [persist]
  timeout_s: 120
  router:
    timeout_s: 120
  io:
    destinations: [file]
    tail_lines: 50

# ─── hydrate (first in flow, ADR-050 §7 / ADR-059 §3) ────────────────────────
# Pulls prior artifacts for this issue out of zbuild/state/issue-<N> so each
# stage's prior-output seam can seed from earlier work. Runs BEFORE intake, and
# is NOT always-run — there is nothing to hydrate at the end of a run.
