id: deployed
name: Deployed Pipeline
extends: simple

# ─── Inheritance note ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# This template is the simple pipeline extended with post-PR delivery stages.
# The engine does not auto-merge shipped templates, so all stages from simple.yaml
# are reproduced here plus deploy → validate → monitor appended after pr.
# merge_policy inherited from simple (auto_unless_flagged).

# ADR-037 §4: per-template merge policy.
merge_policy: auto_unless_flagged

defaults:
  strategy: map

# ─── Flow ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Full simple pipeline + post-PR delivery: deploy → validate → monitor.
# All three post-PR stages are ADR-018 Pattern 1 (one-shot) leaf stages.
flow:
  - hydrate
  - intake
  - plan
  - delivery_loop
  - review_lenses
  - pr
  - deploy
  - validate
  - monitor

# ─── always_run (#1831) ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Stages that run on EVERY exit path — success, non-zero rc, SIGINT, SIGTERM,
# timeout — in the order listed, after the flow has ended.
#
# This replaces a hardcoded dispatch in the runner's EXIT trap, which named one
# plugin by DIRECTORY (`plugins/tool/teardown`) and degraded silently to a no-op
# if it was absent. "Runs on every exit path" is a property of the FLOW, so it
# belongs in the template that defines the flow — not at a line number inside a
# 3000-line runner, where an edit can drop it without anything noticing. #1878
# found exactly that failure in the sibling mechanism: the snapshot was never
# called.
#
# An always-run stage is NOT part of `flow:` and never enters the flow's stage
# list: it has no place in the pipeline's data dependencies and must not affect
# convergence, verdicts, or the run's exit status.
#
# Each entry is an ordinary top-level stage section — resolved by `roles:` like
# any other stage, and bounded by its own `router.timeout_s`. A name here with
# no section, or a section with no `roles:`, REFUSES the template rather than
# quietly running nothing.
always_run:
  - release
  - persist

# ─── delivery_loop (cycle) — #2271, ADR-068; mirrors simple.yaml ────────────
# #2369: design checks its own design.md; a design that still fails ends the
# round, so build does not run on it.
delivery_loop:
  type: cycle
  description: Design, then build, until both pass — going round when a finding needs design
  flow:
    - design
    - build_test_cycle
  exit_when:
    all:
      - { stage: design, field: verdict, op: eq, value: pass }
      - { stage: build_test_cycle, field: verdict, op: eq, value: pass }
  stop_run_on_fail: [design]
  max_iterations: 2
  on_max: halt

# ─── build_test_cycle (cycle) ────────────────────────────────────────────────
build_test_cycle:
  type: cycle
  description: Build, test, and run the mechanical gates until every one passes
  flow:
    # #2371: build scans its own change for secrets (was a stage of its own).
    - build
    - test
  exit_when:
    all:
      # #2371: build must pass — it scans its own change for secrets, and a
      # build that broke scope or did not finish is not done either.
      - { stage: build, field: verdict, op: eq, value: pass }
      - { stage: test, field: verdict, op: eq, value: pass }
  max_iterations: 3
  on_max: continue

# ─── intake (leaf) ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
intake:
  gate: auto
  roles: [intake]
  io:
    destinations: [file, stdout]
    tail_lines: 200

# ─── plan (leaf) ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
plan:
  gate: auto
  roles: [planner]
  # ADR-051: the provider runs the stage as this persona (--agent).
  persona: product-owner
  io:
    destinations: [file, stdout]
    tail_lines: 200
  router:
    timeout_s: 300
    # 45 (raised from the 25 default to match simple.yaml, #1550 / #1442):
    # deployed.yaml fully overrides the plan section so it missed the #1442 bump.
    max_turns: 45

# ─── design (leaf, delivery_loop member) ───────────────────────────────
design:
  gate: auto
  roles: [designer]
  # The whole stage, every call and check inside it (one 10-minute design call
  # and a 10-minute coverage call, plus a few minutes); the engine stops it
  # here. Each run is a new stage, with its own limit. The default is 900.
  timeout_s: 1500
  # ADR-068 §8: a run whose design cannot be used is run again, handed its
  # failures and the last good design — 3 runs in all.
  retry: 2
  # ADR-051: the provider runs the stage as this persona (--agent).
  persona: architect
  io:
    destinations: [file, stdout]
    tail_lines: 200
  router:
    timeout_s: 600
    max_turns: 0

# ─── build (leaf, cycle member) ──────────────────────────────────────────────
build:
  gate: auto
  roles: [builder]
  # The whole stage, every call and check inside it (3 rounds of 15-minute model calls, and more); the engine
  # stops it here. The default for a stage is 900 (15 minutes).
  timeout_s: 3600
  # ADR-051: the provider runs the stage as this persona (--agent).
  persona: developer
  io:
    destinations: [file, stdout]
    tail_lines: 200
  router:
    timeout_s: 900
    max_turns: 0

# ─── test (leaf, cycle member) ───────────────────────────────────────────────
test:
  gate: auto
  roles: [tester]
  # #2372: test runs the shape floor and the acceptance check over its own run,
  # and checks the assertion files against their fingerprints. ADR-036 #1188:
  # negctl_timeout_s bounds each requirement's negative-control / reachability
  # run (seconds).
  negctl_timeout_s: 60
  # The whole stage, every call and check inside it (the full test suite); the engine
  # stops it here. The default for a stage is 900 (15 minutes).
  timeout_s: 2700
  io:
    destinations: [file, stdout]
    tail_lines: 200

# ─── review_lenses (map group, ADVISORY) ─────────────────────────────────────
review_lenses:
  type: map
  # #2368: a lens fails on a problem the change introduced of these severities.
  fail_on: [high, critical]
  over: lenses
  # ADR-051 §2: each lens names the persona it runs as; none is inferred
  # from the lens's name.
  elements:
    - id: security
      persona: security
    - id: performance
      persona: performance
    - id: red-team
      persona: red-team
    - id: correctness
      persona: correctness
    - id: scope
      persona: scope
    - id: sre
      persona: sre
  roles: [review_lens]
  as: ZBUILD_REVIEW_LENS_ID
  max_parallel: 4
  on_member_error: continue
  aggregate: advisory
  io:
    destinations: [file]
    tail_lines: 200
  router:
    timeout_s: 300
    max_turns: 25

# ─── pr (leaf) ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
pr:
  gate: auto
  roles: [pr]
  io:
    destinations: [file, stdout]
    tail_lines: 200

# ─── deploy (leaf) ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# ADR-018 Pattern 1 (one-shot): guard gate verdict → delegate to deploy-release tool.
# T2 agent (kind:agent); no LLM call. Fail-closed: deploys only when every loop passed.
deploy:
  gate: auto
  roles: [deploy_agent]
  io:
    destinations: [file, stdout]
    tail_lines: 200

# ─── validate (leaf) ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# ADR-018 Pattern 1 (one-shot): read deploy-result → health-check probe → done.
# T2 agent (kind:agent); no LLM call.
validate:
  gate: auto
  roles: [validate_agent]
  io:
    destinations: [file, stdout]
    tail_lines: 200

# ─── monitor (leaf) ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# ADR-018 Pattern 1 (one-shot): one-shot LLM health assessment (T1). Reads
# deploy-result.json and pr-url.txt (both optional). Advisory by placement.
monitor:
  gate: auto
  roles: [monitor]
  # ADR-013: monitor is non-blocking — a monitor that cannot reach its target
  # degrades; it does not fail a run whose change already shipped. A leaf's
  # failing verdict otherwise ends the run (#1798).
  blocking: false
  io:
    destinations: [file, stdout]
    tail_lines: 200
  router:
    timeout_s: 300
    max_turns: 10

# ─── release (always-run, ADR-054 §7) ────────────────────────────────────────
# Frees live resources — process groups, locks, handles — and DELETES NOTHING,
# so a failed run keeps every byte of its evidence on disk. The teardown plugin
# pins its own scope to `release`; `purge` is operator-only and unreachable from
# any run path (`zbuild clean --purge`).
#
# timeout_s is 30 and is load-bearing, not a formality: this stage runs inside
# the EXIT trap, so a cleanup hook that blocks would turn Ctrl-C into a hang —
# the exact class of bug the mechanism exists to prevent.
release:
  gate: auto
  roles: [teardown]
  timeout_s: 30
  router:
    timeout_s: 30
  io:
    destinations: [file]
    tail_lines: 50

# ─── persist (always-run, ADR-050 §7 / ADR-059 §3) ───────────────────────────
# Snapshots the artifact area to zbuild/state/issue-<N> and PUSHES it, on every
# exit path. Runs AFTER release, and that order is load-bearing: release frees
# live resources and must stay fast, while this does network I/O and can block
# on auth or a dead remote. Persist last means a bad network can never delay an
# abort.
#
# timeout_s is 120, four times release's 30. A push crosses the network; a
# process-group kill does not.
persist:
  gate: auto
  roles: [persist]
  timeout_s: 120
  router:
    timeout_s: 120
  io:
    destinations: [file]
    tail_lines: 50

# ─── hydrate (first in flow, ADR-050 §7 / ADR-059 §3) ────────────────────────
# Pulls prior artifacts for this issue out of zbuild/state/issue-<N> so each
# stage's prior-output seam can seed from earlier work. Runs BEFORE intake, and
# is NOT always-run — there is nothing to hydrate at the end of a run.
#
# It fetches origin's copy first, which is what makes a fresh CI clone able to
# restore at all; a LOCAL snapshot still wins on read, because it may carry work
# an earlier push never delivered.
hydrate:
  gate: auto
  roles: [hydrate]
  # #2366: restoring less than all earlier work is reported as fail; the run
  # carries on without it rather than stopping.
  blocking: false
  router:
    timeout_s: 60
  io:
    destinations: [file]
    tail_lines: 50

build_run() {
    printf '%s\n' "$BASHPID" > "${BUILD_STARTED:-/dev/null}"
    if [[ "${BUILD_SLEEP:-0}" == "1" ]]; then
        local _i; for _i in $(seq 1 300); do sleep 0.1; done
    fi
    local _art; _art="${ZBUILD_ARTIFACT_DIR:-$(dirname "$2")/artifacts}"; mkdir -p "$_art"
    [[ "${BUILD_ARM_ABORT:-0}" == "1" ]] && : > "${ZBUILD_STATE_DIR}/.abort.signal"
    if [[ "${BUILD_RC:-0}" == "0" ]]; then
        printf '%s' '{"result_contract":3,"outcome":"pass","reason":"stub"}' > "$_art/build-result.json"
    else
        printf '%s' '{"result_contract":3,"outcome":"broken","reason":"stub failure"}' > "$_art/build-result.json"
    fi
    return "${BUILD_RC:-0}"
}
build_cleanup() {
    printf 'build:%s\n' "${3:-NOSCOPE}" >> "${RELEASE_MARKER}"
    # A hook that never returns — used to prove the dispatch is bounded. It
    # records its own pid so SPEC-6 can check it does not outlive the run (#2287).
    if [[ "${BLOCK_CLEANUP:-0}" == "1" ]]; then
        printf '%s\n' "$BASHPID" >> "${RELEASE_MARKER%/*}/hook.pid"
        sleep 120
    fi
    if [[ "${BLOCK_CLEANUP_IGNORE_TERM:-0}" == "1" ]]; then
        # #2333: a child that ignores TERM, under a hook shell that does not.
        ( trap '' TERM; printf '%s\n' "$BASHPID" >> "${RELEASE_MARKER%/*}/hook-child.pid"; sleep 120 ) &
        wait
    fi
    return 0
}
PLUG
cat > "$PLUGINS_ROOT/tool/test/plugin.sh" <<'PLUG'
test_run() {
    local _art; _art="${ZBUILD_ARTIFACT_DIR:-$(dirname "$2")/artifacts}"; mkdir -p "$_art"
    printf '%s' '{"result_contract":3,"outcome":"pass","reason":"stub"}' > "$_art/test-result.json"
    return 0
}
test_cleanup() { printf 'test:%s\n' "${3:-NOSCOPE}" >> "${RELEASE_MARKER}"; return 0; }
PLUG

export ZBUILD_SCOPE_OVERRIDE=1
mkdir -p "$HOME/.zbuild"

_case_no=0
# _prep <name> — fresh state dir + marker for one exit path.
_prep() {
    _case_no=$((_case_no + 1))
    CASE_DIR="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/case-$_case_no-$1"
    mkdir -p "$CASE_DIR/state" "$CASE_DIR/events"
    export ZBUILD_STATE_DIR="$CASE_DIR/state"
    export ZBUILD_EVENTS_DIR="$CASE_DIR/events"
    export ZBUILD_EVENTS_JSONL="$CASE_DIR/events/events.jsonl"
    export RELEASE_MARKER="$CASE_DIR/release-marker"
    export BUILD_STARTED="$CASE_DIR/build-started"

# _assert_released <case> <stage>... — EVERY named stage released, purge never.
#
# #1989: this used to grep the shared marker for any ':release' and pass. Three
# stages append to that one file, so one stage releasing masked two that never
# did — measured: neutering build_cleanup alone left the suite green, and it
# took neutering all three to turn it red. The assertion could only ever detect
# a TOTAL failure of the mechanism, never a partial one, which is the shape a
# real regression takes (#1748: suites observed alive 15+ min after exit).
#
# Each case now names the stages whose cleanup must have run. The sets differ
# by exit path because a stage only reaches release once it has been dispatched.
#
# ADR-062 §2: reclamation reads the process group recorded at DISPATCH, not the
# completion status map, so a stage killed mid-flight IS reclaimable. SPEC-4 and
# SPEC-5 therefore expect `build` as well as `intake` — build had demonstrably
# started (it wrote BUILD_STARTED) before the signal landed. Before #2001 both
# freed `intake` only, because teardown iterated `.stage_statuses`, which
# `_update_stage_status` writes only on complete/failed — i.e. after a stage
# returns, which a killed stage never does.
_assert_released() {
    local _case="$1"; shift
    local _marker; _marker="$(cat "$RELEASE_MARKER" 2>/dev/null || true)"
    local _stage _missing=""
    for _stage in "$@"; do
        grep -q "^${_stage}:release$" <<< "$_marker" || _missing="${_missing}${_stage} "
    done
    if [[ -z "$_missing" ]]; then
        assert_pass "[$_case] cleanup dispatched with scope=release for: $*"
    else
        assert_fail "[$_case] cleanup dispatched with scope=release for: $*" \
            "no release from: ${_missing}| marker=$(tr '\n' ' ' <<< "$_marker")"
    fi
    if grep -q ':purge' <<< "$_marker"; then
        assert_fail "[$_case] purge is never reachable from a run" "marker contained purge"
    else
        assert_pass "[$_case] purge is never reachable from a run"
    fi
}

# SPEC-6 and SPEC-6b each wait out the release bound on purpose: their hook
# blocks, and the bound (the base template's release `timeout_s:` at the
# top-level stage block, 30s after #1801) is what ends it. Started here, each
# from its own repo, so that bound runs while SPEC-1..5 do; their assertions
# are made below, in order.
#

# exits in ~5s. Started here so it runs in parallel with SPEC-6/6b.

name: Resume Minimal Pipeline
extends: simple
defaults:

# Minimal 3-leaf roster (#1098, PC5): the resume-after-SIGINT contract
# (full-pipeline-sigint resume path, Wave 15-E #685) is NOT stage-count
# dependent — it needs only: a stage BEFORE build (intake) to prove resume
# skips an already-complete stage, the build stage that SIGINTs / re-runs,
# and a stage AFTER build (test) to prove resume continues past build.
# Replaces the full ~14-stage standard roster the test used to register so
# the two real subprocess runs (SIGINT + --resume) drive far fewer dispatch
# units. Linear flow, no cycles (resume logic is the same either way).
#
# #1270: this is a per-repo `.zbuild/templates/` overlay (extends: simple).
# When merged over the base, the resulting file carries BOTH the base `flow:`
# and this `stages:` list, so the loader treats it as OLD-shape and honors ONLY
# the stages below (the base roster is discarded — it just has to exist).
#
# Stages declare NO `roles:` block on purpose. With roles, the runner routes
# the stage through the fanout strategy (orch pool), which collapses a child
# rc=130 into a generic rc=1 — that would break the SIGINT-propagation
# contract (build returns 130 → runner must exit 130). Without roles, the
# runner resolves the plugin by stage ID and calls plugin_hook_call directly,
# preserving the leaf's exact rc (the same effective dispatch the standard
# template gets via cycle_dispatch_stage for its cycle-member build).
stages:
  - id: intake
    gate: auto
    io:
      destinations: [file, stdout]

    gate: auto
    io:

id: always-run-minimal
name: Always-Run Minimal Pipeline
extends: simple
defaults:
  strategy: fanout

# #1831 fixture: the smallest template that exercises `always_run:`.
#
# NEW shape (`flow:` + top-level sections) on purpose — but NOT because
# `always_run:` needs it. The key is shape-INDEPENDENT: `_tpl_parse_always_run`
# reads it straight from the file, and SPEC-6 in tests/unit/template-always-run-test.sh
# proves an old-shape template inherits it too. The new shape is used here only
# because it is the smaller fixture, and because it exercises the per-repo
# overlay's new-shape path alongside it.
#
# `outcome` is the only flow stage. Its plugin is replaced per-case by the test
# so one fixture can drive every exit path: rc=0, rc=1, SIGINT (rc=130), SIGTERM
# and a hang past the timeout. `release` is never in the flow — the whole point
# is that it runs anyway.
flow:
  - outcome

always_run:
  - release

outcome:
  gate: auto
  io:
    destinations: [file]
    tail_lines: 50

# timeout_s is deliberately small so the watchdog case does not stretch the
# suite's wall clock. The bound itself is what SPEC-5 asserts.
release:
  gate: auto
  roles: [teardown]
  router:
    timeout_s: 2
  io:
    destinations: [file]
    tail_lines: 50

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# tests/unit/lint-test-errexit-test.sh — a test file that runs without
# stop-on-error never turns it on (#2252 G).
#
# Why: #1844 run 36969128968 — test-author wrapped a call in `set +e … set -e`
# inside pr-pipeline-test.sh, a file that runs `set -uo pipefail` (no -e). The
# `set -e` switched errexit ON for the rest of the file, so the next assertion
# that expected rc=1 killed the script; build could not edit the authored test,
# so the iteration could never pass.
#
# L1 [change] a file whose header has no -e and later runs `set -e` is refused
# L2 [change] ...also `set -euo pipefail` mid-file
# L3 [guard]  a file that starts with -e may toggle it (set +e … set -e)
# L4 [guard]  `set +e` alone, or `set -o pipefail`, is fine
# L5 [guard]  the real tree passes
set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)"
# shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/helpers.sh
source "$REPO_ROOT/scripts/lib/helpers.sh"
# shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/test-helpers.sh
source "$REPO_ROOT/scripts/lib/test-helpers.sh"
print_test_header "a test file never turns stop-on-error on mid-file (#2252 G)"
setup_test_env "lint-test-errexit"
LINT="$REPO_ROOT/scripts/lib/lint-test-errexit.sh"
T="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/tree/tests"; mkdir -p "$T"
_lint() { bash "$LINT" "$TEST_TEMP_DIR/tree" >/dev/null 2>&1; echo $?; }
_file() { printf '%s\n' "$@" > "$T/x-test.sh"; }

_file '#!/usr/bin/env bash' 'set -uo pipefail' 'set +e' 'cmd' 'set -e' 'assert'
assert_eq "[L1] no -e header, then set -e → refused" "1" "$(_lint)"
_file '#!/usr/bin/env bash' 'set -uo pipefail' 'set -euo pipefail'
assert_eq "[L2] ...set -euo pipefail mid-file → refused" "1" "$(_lint)"
_file '#!/usr/bin/env bash' 'set -euo pipefail' 'set +e' 'cmd' 'set -e'
assert_eq "[L3] an -e header may toggle it" "0" "$(_lint)"
_file '#!/usr/bin/env bash' 'set -uo pipefail' 'set +e' 'set -o pipefail'
assert_eq "[L4] set +e and set -o pipefail are fine" "0" "$(_lint)"
_real="$(bash "$LINT" 2>&1)"; _rc=$?
assert_eq "[L5] the real tree passes" "0" "$_rc"
[[ "$_rc" -eq 0 ]] || printf '%s\n' "$_real" >&2

cleanup_test_env
print_test_results
exit $((FAIL > 0))
